title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise Performance: With a Focus on Vitamin E and C Supplementation
authors: Madalyn Riley Higgins, Azimeh Izadi, Mojtaba Kaviani
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This paper reviews antioxidant supplementation, specifically vitamins E and C, for exercise performance. Evidence suggests supplementation may hinder exercise adaptations and is generally not beneficial, except in specific circumstances.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Effect of high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle recovery and training adaptation: a mini review
authors: Jooyoung Kim
abstract: This review examined high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle recovery and training adaptation. Evidence suggests potential negative impacts on adaptation, with unclear benefits for recovery.

title: Antioxidant supplements and endurance exercise: Current evidence and mechanistic insights
authors: Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Lewan Parker, Glenn D. Wadley
abstract: This review examines antioxidant supplements for endurance athletes. Most supplements lack evidence for performance enhancement, with some potentially hindering training adaptations.

title: The Effects of Strength Training Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Maurilio T. Dutra, Wagner Rodrigues Martins, Alexandre L. A. Ribeiro, Martim Bottaro
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined studies on vitamin C and E supplementation combined with strength training. The findings suggest these supplements do not enhance muscle strength or mass and may even attenuate hypertrophy.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Do Antioxidant Vitamins Prevent Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage? A Systematic Review
authors: María Martinez-Ferran, Fabian Sanchis-Gomar, Carl J. Lavie, Giuseppe Lippi, Helios Pareja-Galeano
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle damage. The available data are not conclusive regarding whether these vitamins prevent muscle damage.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: Supplementation with Vitamins C and E and Exercise-Induced Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review
authors: María F. Torre, María Martinez-Ferran, Néstor Vallecillo, Sergio L. Jiménez, Carlos Romero-Morales, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effect on exercise-induced muscle soreness. The evidence is insufficient to confirm these vitamins minimize delayed-onset muscle soreness.

title: Dietary thiols in exercise: oxidative stress defence, exercise performance, and adaptation
authors: Yanita McLeay, Stephen Stannard, Stuart Houltham, Carlene Starck
abstract: This paper reviews dietary thiols, focusing on their role in exercise-induced oxidative stress defense and performance. It suggests that thiol donors, like keratin, may enhance antioxidant capacity and performance without negatively impacting training adaptations.

title: Vitamin C and glutathione supplementation: a review of their additive effects on exercise performance
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
abstract: This review examined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation's effects on exercise performance. Combined supplementation's additive effects are anticipated but remain largely unexplored and require further study.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Hinders the Role of Exercise Training as a Natural Activator of SIRT1
authors: Carmine Sellitto, Graziamaria Corbi, Berenice Stefanelli, Valentina Manzo, Marta Trucillo, Bruno Cha...
abstract: Exercise training increases SIRT1 levels, which boosts the body's antioxidant system. However, antioxidant supplements appear to interfere with this exercise-induced activation of SIRT1.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.

title: A Vitamin E-Enriched Antioxidant Diet Interferes with the Acute Adaptation of the Liver to Physical Exercise in Mice
authors: Miriam Hoene, Martin Irmler, Johannes Beckers, Martin Hrabě de Angelis, Hans-Ulrich Häring, Cora Wei...
abstract: A study examined how a vitamin E-enriched diet affects the liver's response to exercise in mice. High vitamin E intake disrupted the liver's normal metabolic and inflammatory adaptations to physical activity.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Effects of vitamins C and E supplementation combined with 12-week resistance training in older women with sarcopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Xu Liu, Bo Chen, Yutian Jin, Feiyan Zhong, Yunjuan Zhang, Yu Li, Yun Zhang, Runhong Cui, Bing Wu, Cu...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C, E, and resistance training in older women with sarcopenia. Supplementation with vitamins C and E enhanced muscle mass and strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Potential harms of supplementation with high doses of antioxidants in athletes
authors: Shunchang Li, Babatunde Fasipe, Ismail Laher
abstract: This paper reviews the use of high-dose antioxidant supplements by athletes. It concludes that these supplements may hinder beneficial training adaptations and potentially cause harm.

title: Supplementation with α-Lipoic Acid, CoQ10, and Vitamin E Augments Running Performance and Mitochondrial Function in Female Mice
authors: Arkan Abadi, Justin D. Crane, Daniel Ogborn, Bart Hettinga, Mahmood Akhtar, Andrew Stokl, Lauren Mac...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an antioxidant cocktail on running performance and mitochondrial function in mice. The supplement improved performance and mitochondrial function in untrained female mice, but not in trained mice.

title: Antioxidants and Sports Performance
authors: Vicente Javier Clemente-Suárez, Álvaro Bustamante-Sanchez, Juan Mielgo-Ayuso, Ismael Martínez-Guarda...
abstract: This review analyzes the role of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant responses in sports performance and training adaptations. ROS production during exercise significantly impacts performance, and antioxidants can aid recovery and performance.

title: Influence of Vitamin C Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Neutrophil Inflammatory Response in Acute and Regular Exercise
authors: Ljiljana M. Popovic, Nebojsa R. Mitic, Dijana Miric, Boban Bisevac, Mirjana Miric, Brankica Popovic
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's impact on oxidative stress and neutrophil inflammation from exercise. Vitamin C supplementation reduced exercise-induced lipid peroxidation but did not affect neutrophil inflammatory response.

title: Elevated hepcidin serum level in response to inflammatory and iron signals in exercising athletes is independent of moderate supplementation with vitamin C and E
authors: Víctor Díaz, Ana B Peinado, Laura Barba-Moreno, Sandro Altamura, Javier Butragueño, Marcela González...
abstract: This study investigated hepcidin levels in athletes after exercise. Hepcidin remained elevated despite vitamin C and E supplementation, indicating these vitamins do not alter the response to inflammatory and iron signals.

title: A Comparison of the Antioxidant Effects Between Hydrogen Gas Inhalation and Vitamin C Supplementation in Response to a 60-Min Treadmill Exercise in Rat Gastrocnemius Muscle
authors: Li Chaoqun, Zhao Yuqi, Zhou Shi, Yu Zhenghui, Wen Li
abstract: Hydrogen gas inhalation and vitamin C were compared for their antioxidant effects on rat gastrocnemius muscle after treadmill exercise. Hydrogen gas reduced oxidative stress without blunting mitochondrial biogenesis signals, unlike vitamin C.

title: Vitamin C, A and E supplementation decreases the expression of  HSPA1A  and  HSPB1  genes in the leukocytes of young polish figure skaters during a 10-day training camp
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Zbigniew Jastrzębski, Grzegorz Chruściński, Monika Michałowska–Sawczyn, Alicja...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin A, C, and E supplementation on gene expression in young figure skaters during a training camp. Supplementation significantly decreased the expression of stress-related genes HSPA1A and HSPB1 in leukocytes.

title: Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Performance: “Common Knowledge” vs. Experimental Evidence
authors: Andrés Hernández, Arthur Cheng, Håkan Westerblad
abstract: This paper reviews experimental evidence on the effects of antioxidants on skeletal muscle performance. Findings suggest that common beliefs about antioxidant benefits may not be supported by scientific data and could potentially be harmful.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on renal non-enzymatic antioxidants in young rats submitted to exhaustive exercise stress
authors: Sérvio A Bucioli, Luiz Carlos de Abreu, Vitor E Valenti, Claudio Leone, Helio Vannucchi
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effects on renal antioxidants in young rats undergoing exhaustive exercise. Vitamin E supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and increased antioxidant levels in the kidneys.

title: Resistance-based training improves mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in aging adults, independent of polyphenol supplementation
authors: Mathias Flensted-Jensen, Cecilie Moe Weinreich, Ann-Sofie Kleis-Olsen, Filip Hansen, Nadia Stenner S...
abstract: Resistance training improved mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in older adults. Polyphenol supplementation did not enhance these adaptations and may have altered some vitamin responses.

title: Vitamin A Oral Supplementation Induces Oxidative Stress and Suppresses IL-10 and HSP70 in Skeletal Muscle of Trained Rats
authors: Lyvia Lintzmaier Petiz, Carolina Saibro Girardi, Rafael Calixto Bortolin, Alice Kunzler, Juciano Gas...
abstract: Vitamin A supplementation was studied in trained rats. It impaired exercise-induced antioxidant capacity and suppressed anti-inflammatory responses in skeletal muscle.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation and high intensity interval training induced changes in lipid profile and haematological variables of young males
authors: Surojit Sarkar, Swapan Kr Dey, Gouriprosad Datta, Amit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in young males. Supplementation protected against negative hematological changes and improved lipid profiles and explosive strength without affecting endurance.

title: Exercise Training and Skeletal Muscle Antioxidant Enzymes: An Update
authors: Scott K. Powers, Erica Goldstein, Matthew Schrager, Li Li Ji
abstract: This review summarizes how endurance, interval, and resistance exercise training increase skeletal muscle antioxidant enzymes. This upregulation protects against exercise-induced oxidative damage, potentially delaying fatigue and improving performance.

title: Can Low-Dose of Dietary Vitamin E Supplementation Reduce Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress? A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Myunghee Kim, Hyeyoon Eo, Josephine Gahyun Lim, Hyunjung Lim, Yunsook Lim
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effects of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage. Low-dose vitamin E, especially under 500 IU, was found to reduce muscle damage, particularly in athletes.

title: The effect of an acute antioxidant supplementation compared with placebo on performance and hormonal response during a high volume resistance training session
authors: James Ackerman, Tom Clifford, Lars R McNaughton, David J Bentley
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: An antioxidant supplement was compared to a placebo before a high-volume resistance training session. The antioxidant group showed improved muscle performance and a blunted growth hormone response.

title: An Overview of Physical Exercise and Antioxidant Supplementation Influences on Skeletal Muscle Oxidative Stress
authors: Shima Taherkhani, Kosar Valaei, Hamid Arazi, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This paper reviews how exercise and antioxidant supplements affect skeletal muscle oxidative stress. Findings are paradoxical due to varied study designs, necessitating further research.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Effect of vitamin E (Tri E ® ) on antioxidant enzymes and DNA damage in rats following eight weeks exercise
authors: Noor Aini Abd Hamid, Mohd A Hasrul, Rusdiah J Ruzanna, Ibrahim A Ibrahim, Prasamit S Baruah, Musalma...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation on antioxidant enzymes and DNA damage in rats undergoing exercise. Vitamin E supplementation reduced DNA damage in exercising rats, likely due to enhanced antioxidant defense.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise: A Redox-Informed Framework for Training Adaptation, Performance, and Recovery
authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu; Andrei Tudor; Andreea Maria Mănescu; Iulius Radulian Mărgărit; Cătălin Octavia...
abstract: Antioxidants can hinder training adaptations by blunting exercise-induced signals. However, certain food-derived antioxidants may aid recovery without impairing gains. A framework called Redox-Adaptive Periodization is proposed to optimize antioxidant use based on training goals.

title: Exhaustive exercise and vitamins C and E modulate thyroid hormone levels at low and high altitudes
authors: Fahaid Al-Hashem, Mahmoud Alkhateeb, Bahjat Al-Ani, Hussein Sakr, Mohammad Khalil
abstract: Exhaustive exercise and vitamin C/E supplementation were studied in rats at low and high altitudes. The study found that exercise and antioxidants increased thyroid hormones, with reduced T4 to T3 conversion.

title: Enhancing Supplemental Effects of Acute Natural Antioxidant Derived from Yeast Fermentation and Vitamin C on Sports Performance in Triathlon Athletes: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Yerin Sun, Jae-Ho Choi, Jisoo Seo, Yanghoon Peter Jung, Ah...
abstract: This study examined the effects of combined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation on middle-aged triathletes during exercise. The combination improved metabolic, skeletal muscle oxygenation, cardiac, and antioxidant functions compared to individual supplements or placebo.

title: Enhanced Antioxidative Defense by Vitamins C and E Consumption Prevents 7-Day High-Salt Diet-Induced Microvascular Endothelial Function Impairment in Young Healthy Individuals
authors: Lidija Barić, Ines Drenjančević, Martina Mihalj, Anita Matić, Marko Stupin, Luka Kolar, Zrinka Mihal...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamins C and E prevent high-salt diet-induced microvascular dysfunction in healthy individuals. The findings show these vitamins prevented the diet's negative effects on endothelial function by mitigating oxidative stress.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and the Effects of Antioxidant Intake from a Physiological Viewpoint
authors: Takuji Kawamura, Isao Muraoka
abstract: This review examines exercise-induced oxidative stress and the impact of antioxidant intake in healthy individuals. It finds that while exercise increases reactive oxygen species, antioxidant supplementation's effects are extensively studied but complex.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and Dietary Antioxidants
authors: Abbas Yavari, Maryam Javadi, Parvin Mirmiran, Zahra Bahadoran
abstract: This review examined evidence on antioxidant supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. A balanced diet rich in natural antioxidants is recommended over supplementation for athletes.

title: Creatine supplementation post-exercise does not enhance training-induced adaptations in middle to older aged males
authors: Matthew B. Cooke, Brian Brabham, Thomas W. Buford, Brian D. Shelmadine, Matthew McPheeters, Geoffrey...
abstract: This study investigated creatine supplementation post-exercise in older males undergoing resistance training. Creatine did not enhance training-induced gains in body composition or muscle strength compared to placebo.

title: Antioxidative properties of phenolic compounds and their effect on oxidative stress induced by severe physical exercise
authors: Joanna Kruk, Basil Hassan Aboul-Enein, Ewa Duchnik, Mariola Marchlewicz
abstract: This paper reviews phenolic compounds' antioxidant properties and their impact on exercise-induced oxidative stress. Phenolic compounds can reduce exercise-induced oxidative stress and inflammation, but their effect on physical performance is inconsistent.

title: Vitamin D 3  supplementation does not enhance the effects of resistance training in older adults
authors: Knut Sindre Mølmen, Daniel Hammarström, Karianne Pedersen, Anne Cecilie Lian Lie, Ragnvald B. Steile...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation on resistance training outcomes in older adults. Vitamin D3 supplementation did not enhance improvements in muscle strength, mass, or endurance compared to placebo.

title: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a mixture of vitamin C and vitamin E for endurance capacity in a double blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Seung Wan Kang, Seokyung Hahn, Jung-Kyu Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Byung-Joo Park, Sang Chul Lee
abstract: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a vitamin C/E mixture were tested for endurance effects in exercising males. OLFE significantly improved running time and anaerobic threshold, while the vitamin mixture unexpectedly reduced VO2 max.

title: Elastic resistance training is more effective than vitamin D3 supplementation in reducing oxidative stress and strengthen antioxidant enzymes in healthy men
authors: Fardin Kalvandi, Mohammad Ali Azarbayjani, Ronak Azizbeigi, Kamal Azizbeigi
abstract: Elastic resistance training was studied with and without vitamin D3 supplementation in healthy men. Elastic resistance training alone was more effective than with vitamin D3 supplementation for reducing oxidative stress and strengthening antioxidant enzymes.

title: Exercise performance and physiological responses: the potential role of redox imbalance
authors: Kavey Vidal, Nathaniel Robinson, Stephen J. Ives
abstract: This study investigated the effects of hyperoxia and an antioxidant cocktail on cycling performance and physiological responses. Ingesting an antioxidant cocktail impaired performance, ventilation, and economy, suggesting a disruption of redox balance.

title: Training Enhances Immune Cells Mitochondrial Biosynthesis, Fission, Fusion, and Their Antioxidant Capabilities Synergistically with Dietary Docosahexaenoic Supplementation
authors: Carla Busquets-Cortés, Xavier Capó, Miquel Martorell, Josep A. Tur, Antoni Sureda, Antoni Pons
abstract: Training and DHA supplementation increased mitochondrial proteins and activity in immune cells. This combined intervention enhanced mitochondrial function more than training alone.

title: Effect of vitamin E succinate on inflammatory cytokines induced by high-intensity interval training
authors: Hadi Sarir, Ghodsieh Emdadifard, Homayoun Farhangfar, Hossein TaheriChadorneshin
source: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences : The Official Journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E succinate's effect on inflammatory cytokines after high-intensity interval training in rats. Vitamin E succinate supplementation reduced HIIT-induced increases in IL-6 and TNF-α.

title: Use of Saliva Biomarkers to Monitor Efficacy of Vitamin C in Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress
authors: Levi W. Evans, Stanley T. Omaye
abstract: This review examines the use of saliva biomarkers to monitor vitamin C's efficacy against exercise-induced oxidative stress. Saliva shows promise as a non-invasive biospecimen for reflecting systemic oxidative stress and antioxidant status.

title: Reactive oxygen species in exercise and insulin resistance: Working towards personalized antioxidant treatment
authors: Kathryn McKeegan, Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Michelle A. Keske, Glenn D. Wadley, Paul A. Della ...
abstract: This review examines human research on antioxidant treatment for insulin resistance and glycemic control. Personalized antioxidant strategies are needed, considering context, individual deficiencies, and antioxidant properties, to improve effectiveness.

title: Oxidative Stress, Mitochondrial Function and Adaptation to Exercise: New Perspectives in Nutrition
authors: Nancy Vargas-Mendoza, Marcelo Angeles-Valencia, Ángel Morales-González, Eduardo Osiris Madrigal-Sant...
abstract: This paper reviews how mitochondria adapt to exercise-induced energy demands and oxidative stress. It explores whether nutrients, particularly antioxidants, might interfere with this adaptation or exercise performance.

title: Combination of vitamin E and vitamin C alleviates renal function in hyperoxaluric rats via antioxidant activity
authors: Orapun JATURAKAN, Thasinas DISSAYABUTRA, Narongsak CHAIYABUTR, Anusak KIJTAWORNRAT, Piyaratana TOSUK...
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and C on hyperoxaluric rats. Combined vitamin E and C supplementation protected against oxalate-induced kidney damage by reducing oxidative stress.

title: Oxidants, Antioxidants, and the Beneficial Roles of Exercise-Induced Production of Reactive Species
authors: Elisa Couto Gomes, Albená Nunes Silva, Marta Rubino de Oliveira
abstract: This review examines reactive species produced during exercise and their impact on adaptation. Exercise-induced reactive species promote beneficial adaptations like angiogenesis and muscle growth.

title: (–)-Epicatechin Supplementation Inhibits Aerobic Adaptations to Cycling Exercise in Humans
authors: Neil A. Schwarz, Zachary J. Blahnik, Srihari Prahadeeswaran, Sarah K. McKinley-Barnard, Shelley L. H...
abstract: This study investigated if (–)-epicatechin supplementation enhances cycling training adaptations. The findings indicate that (–)-epicatechin supplementation inhibits aerobic adaptations, specifically peak VO2 and succinate dehydrogenase content, compared to a placebo.

title: Exercise, oxidants, and antioxidants change the shape of the bell-shaped hormesis curve
authors: Zsolt Radak, Kazunari Ishihara, Eva Tekus, Csaba Varga, Aniko Posa, Laszlo Balogh, Istvan Boldogh, E...
abstract: This paper examines how exercise and antioxidant treatments affect the relationship between ROS and physiological function. It concludes that antioxidant timing relative to exercise intensity dictates whether function is attenuated or enhanced, and that fitness influences this response.

title: The effect of green tea extract supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress parameters in male sprinters
authors: Ewa Jówko, Barbara Długołęcka, Beata Makaruk, Igor Cieśliński
abstract: This study investigated the effects of green tea extract on oxidative stress markers in male sprinters. Green tea extract supplementation reduced exercise-induced oxidative stress without negatively impacting sprint performance or antioxidant enzyme adaptation.

title: Antioxidant Effects and Insulin Resistance Improvement of Chromium Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
authors: Ming-Hoang Lai
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of chromium, vitamin C, and E supplementation on type 2 diabetes patients. Combined supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress and improved glucose metabolism.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Markers of Oxidative Stress and Muscle Damage after Strength Exercise: A Systematic Review
authors: Cristina Canals-Garzón, Rafael Guisado-Barrilao, Darío Martínez-García, Ignacio Jesús Chirosa-Ríos, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined antioxidant supplementation's effects on oxidative stress and muscle damage after strength exercise. Antioxidants like pomegranate juice and taurine showed beneficial effects, potentially reducing fatigue and speeding recovery.

title: Polyphenol Supplementation and Antioxidant Status in Athletes: A Narrative Review
authors: Aleksandra Bojarczuk, Magdalena Dzitkowska-Zabielska
abstract: This review examined polyphenol supplementation's effects on athletes' antioxidant status and exercise performance. The available evidence does not conclusively support widespread polyphenol supplementation for athletes, indicating a need for further research.

title: Polyphenol Supplementation: Benefits for Exercise Performance or Oxidative Stress?
authors: Kathryn H. Myburgh
abstract: This review examines polyphenol supplementation's effects on exercise performance and oxidative stress. Current evidence is insufficient to recommend polyphenol use for athletes due to study limitations.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Modulates Neutrophil Inflammatory Response to Exercise-Induced Stress
authors: Lucrecia Carrera-Quintanar, Lorena Funes, María Herranz-López, Pascual Martínez-Peinado, Sandra Pasc...
abstract: This study investigated the inflammatory response to exercise and the effect of antioxidant supplements. Antioxidant supplementation appeared to alter neutrophil inflammatory marker release, potentially influencing post-exercise recovery.

title: Impact of pre‐exercise feeding status on metabolic adaptations to endurance‐type exercise training
authors: Robert M. Edinburgh, Francoise Koumanov, Javier T. Gonzalez
abstract: This study investigated how pre-exercise feeding status affects metabolic adaptations to endurance training. Performing exercise in a fasted state may enhance certain metabolic adaptations compared to exercising after nutrient ingestion.

title: Effects of ascorbic acid supplementation on oxidative stress markers in healthy women following a single bout of exercise
authors: Manita Yimcharoen, Suwatsin Kittikunnathum, Chawannut Suknikorn, Wichuda Nak-on, Petcharee Yeethong,...
abstract: This study investigated ascorbic acid's effects on oxidative stress markers in women after exercise. Ascorbic acid improved antioxidant capacity but did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation and Mitochondria in Experimental and Functional Hyperthyroidism: A Mini-Review
authors: Gaetana Napolitano, Gianluca Fasciolo, Sergio Di Meo, Paola Venditti
abstract: This mini-review examines vitamin E's role in protecting mitochondria from oxidative damage in hyperthyroidism. Vitamin E supplementation limits hyperthyroidism-induced mitochondrial ROS and oxidative damage, preserving cell function.

title: Can vitamin C supplementation reverse the effects of exercise training in polluted air on oxidative stress markers? A randomized controlled trial
authors: Amin Eatemadyboroujeni, Mehdi Kargarfard, Hojatollah Alaei
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise, polluted air, and vitamin C on oxidative stress markers in rats. Vitamin C supplementation did not significantly reverse the increased oxidative stress caused by exercise in polluted air.

title: Effect of Vitamins C and E Co-Supplementation on Serum C-Reactive Protein Level: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Faezeh Fouladvand, Ebrahim Falahi, Omid Asbaghi, Amir Abbasnezhad
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined vitamin C and E co-supplementation's effect on C-reactive protein. Co-supplementation did not significantly impact CRP overall, but reduced it in those aged 30 and over.

title: The Effects of Antioxidant Supplementation on Soccer Performance and Recovery: A Critical Review of the Available Evidence
authors: Athanasios Poulios, Konstantinos Papanikolaou, Dimitrios Draganidis, Panagiotis Tsimeas, Athanasios ...
abstract: This review examined antioxidant supplements' effects on soccer performance and recovery. Several antioxidants were found to reduce muscle damage, inflammation, and oxidative stress, with some potentially enhancing performance.

title: Cashew apple juice supplementation enhanced fat utilization during high-intensity exercise in trained and untrained men
authors: Piyapong Prasertsri, Thapanee Roengrit, Yupaporn Kanpetta, Terdthai Tong-un, Supaporn Muchimapura, J...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Cashew apple juice supplementation was studied for its effect on substrate utilization during high-intensity exercise. CAJ supplementation increased fat oxidation and decreased carbohydrate oxidation during exercise in both trained and untrained men.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of antioxidants with or without exercise training improving muscle condition in older adults
authors: Yijie Wang, Ziping He, Chunye Long, Yue Li, Yuzhe Yuan, Tianlong Huang
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the effects of antioxidants and exercise on muscle condition in older adults. Combining antioxidants with exercise yielded greater improvements in muscle strength and physical function than either intervention alone.

title: The effect of combined resistance exercise training and vitamin D 3  supplementation on musculoskeletal health and function in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Antoniak, Carolyn A Greig
abstract: This systematic review evaluated combined resistance exercise and vitamin D supplementation in older adults. The combination significantly improved lower limb muscle strength compared to exercise alone.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Does Not Enhance Gains in Muscle Strength and Lean Body Mass or Influence Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Vitamin D-Insufficient Middle-Aged Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Evelin Mäestu, Luule Medijainen, Märt Lellsaar, Kri...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D supplementation's effect on resistance training outcomes in vitamin D-insufficient men. Vitamin D supplementation did not enhance muscle strength, lean body mass, or cardiorespiratory fitness gains.

title: Aerobic Exercise Training Adaptations Are Increased by Postexercise Carbohydrate-Protein Supplementation
authors: Lisa Ferguson-Stegall, Erin McCleave, Zhenping Ding, Phillip G. Doerner III, Yang Liu, Bei Wang, Mar...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of post-exercise chocolate milk, carbohydrate, or placebo supplementation on aerobic training adaptations. Chocolate milk supplementation led to greater improvements in aerobic capacity and body composition compared to carbohydrate or placebo.

title: Effects of Vitamin E and Coenzyme Q 10  Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Parameters in Untrained Leisure Horses Subjected to Acute Moderate Exercise
authors: Alenka Nemec Svete, Tomaž Vovk, Mojca Bohar Topolovec, Peter Kruljc
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E and CoQ10 supplementation in untrained horses undergoing exercise. Vitamin E, alone or combined with CoQ10, prevented exercise-induced lipid peroxidation.

title: Synergistic Effects of Exercise Training and Vitamin D Supplementation on Mitochondrial Function of Cardiac Tissue, Antioxidant Capacity, and Tumor Growth in Breast Cancer in Bearing-4T1 Mice
authors: Ali Jafari, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani, Farnoosh Khosrobakhsh, Neda Khaledi
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise and vitamin D on breast cancer mice. Combining exercise and vitamin D inhibited tumor growth, improved antioxidant capacity, and positively modulated cardiac gene expression.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Cardiac Troponin Release in Cyclists: A Randomized Trial
authors: Lieke J. J. Klinkenberg, Peter T. Res, Guido R. Haenen, Aalt Bast, Luc J. C. van Loon, Marja P. van ...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of astaxanthin supplementation on exercise-induced cardiac troponin release in cyclists. Astaxanthin supplementation did not reduce cardiac troponin release after prolonged cycling, nor did it improve antioxidant capacity or markers of muscle damage.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Supplementation with a Multi-ingredient Pre-workout Supplement does not Augment Resistance Training Adaptations in Females
authors: ANNA NELSON, CLAYTON L. CAMIC, CARL FOSTER, BROOKE ZAJAC, KAELA HOECHERL, JACOB ERICKSON, ANDREW R. ...
abstract: This study examined the effects of a multi-ingredient pre-workout supplement on female resistance training adaptations. The supplement did not enhance body composition or strength gains compared to a placebo.

title: The effect of short-term vitamin D on the antioxidant capacity following exhaustive aerobic exercise
authors: Vahid Parvizi Mastali, Rastegar Hoseini, Mohammad Azizi
abstract: This study examined the impact of short-term vitamin D supplementation on antioxidant capacity in inactive men after exhaustive aerobic exercise. Six weeks of vitamin D supplementation significantly enhanced antioxidant enzyme activity and vitamin D levels, suggesting a protective effect against exercise-induced oxidative stress.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: effects of dietary antioxidants on exercise and sports performance
authors: Drew E. Gonzalez; Broderick L. Dickerson; Brandon M. Roberts; Jennifer A. Kurtz; Hunter S. Waldman; ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Following a comprehensive review, the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on the role of dietary antioxidants in exercise and sport. Antioxidants play a

title: Effect of exercise training on saliva brain derived neurotrophic factor, catalase and vitamin c
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Bahram Soltani Tehrani, Yazgaldi Nazari, Reyhaneh Sariri, Rastegar ...
source: Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
abstract: This study examined salivary antioxidants and BDNF in sedentary men after exhaustive exercise. Acute exercise reduced catalase, vitamin C, and BDNF, with BDNF showing a prolonged decrease.

title: Astaxanthin supplementation enhances metabolic adaptation with aerobic training in the elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Ana P. Valencia, Matt P. VanDoren, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan, Kevin E. Co...
abstract: Astaxanthin supplementation was studied alongside aerobic training in elderly adults to assess its impact on metabolic adaptation. The study found astaxanthin enhanced specific muscle endurance and fat oxidation, particularly in males.

title: Vitamin 25(OH)D 3 , E, and C Supplementation Impact the Inflammatory and Antioxidant Responses in Piglets Fed a Deoxynivalenol-Contaminated Diet and Challenged with Lipopolysaccharides
authors: Béatrice Sauvé, Younes Chorfi, Marie-Pierre Létourneau-Montminy, Frédéric Guay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin 25(OH)D₃, E, and C supplementation on piglets fed a deoxynivalenol-contaminated diet and challenged with lipopolysaccharides. Vitamins E and C, or all three vitamins, protected against deoxynivalenol by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation.

title: Effects of vitamin D 3  supplementation on oxidative stress and antioxidant enzyme after strenuous endurance exercise in healthy young men: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Cheng-Tse Yang, Pei-Wei Weng, Li-Hui Chien, Sunil Kumar, Ming-Ta Yang
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D3 supplementation's effects on oxidative stress after endurance exercise. Vitamin D3 supplementation mitigated exercise-induced oxidative stress markers in healthy young men.

title: Acute exercise and oxidative stress: a 30 year history
authors: Kelsey Fisher-Wellman, Richard J Bloomer
abstract: Acute exercise can induce oxidative stress, with its extent influenced by exercise and subject factors. This stress, however, appears to be a necessary stimulus for enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses.

title: Effect of Vitamins A, C, and E Supplementation in the Treatment of Metabolic Syndrome in Albino Rats
authors: L. S. Bilbis, S. A. Muhammad, Y. Saidu, Y. Adamu
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamins A, C, and E on metabolic syndrome in rats fed a high-salt diet. Vitamin supplementation significantly reduced blood pressure, improved lipid profiles, and increased antioxidant status, suggesting a protective role.

title: Modification of the Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on the Mortality of Male Smokers by Age and Dietary Vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: Vitamin E supplementation's effect on mortality in male smokers was examined. Its impact varied significantly by age and dietary vitamin C intake, suggesting heterogeneous effects in different population subgroups.

title: The effects of physical training on antioxidative status under exercise-induced oxidative stress
authors: Eun-Young Choi, Youn-Ok Cho
abstract: Physical training's effects on antioxidant status and lipid profiles under exercise-induced oxidative stress were studied in rats. Moderate training enhances antioxidant defenses and reduces the atherosclerotic index, especially during and after exercise.

title: Astaxanthin Supplementation as a Potential Strategy for Enhancing Mitochondrial Adaptations in the Endurance Athlete: An Invited Review
authors: Hunter Waldman
abstract: This review examines astaxanthin's potential to enhance mitochondrial adaptations in endurance athletes. Findings suggest astaxanthin may improve performance, recovery, and antioxidant capacity when combined with training.

title: Role of creatine supplementation on exercise-induced cardiovascular function and oxidative stress
authors: Michael IC Kingsley, Daniel Cunningham, Laura Mason, Liam P Kilduff, Jane McEneny
abstract: This study investigated creatine supplementation's effects on oxidative stress markers after exhaustive cycling. Creatine supplementation did not improve antioxidant defenses or reduce exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in healthy males.

title: Targeted Antioxidants in Exercise-Induced Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress: Emphasis on DNA Damage
authors: Josh Williamson, Gareth Davison
abstract: This review examines mitochondria-targeted antioxidants and their potential to mitigate exercise-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, particularly DNA damage. Targeted antioxidants offer a promising approach to address this damage, unlike non-selective antioxidants.

title: The Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Fatigue during Exercise: Potential Role for NAD + (H)
authors: John Mach, Adrian W. Midgley, Steve Dank, Ross S. Grant, David J. Bentley
abstract: This study investigated the impact of antioxidant supplementation on exercise fatigue and NAD+ levels. Antioxidant supplementation increased exercise time to fatigue and serum NAD+ levels, suggesting reduced oxidative stress improved aerobic respiration.

title: Skeletal Muscle Redox Signaling in Health and Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Exercise Strategies
authors: Hyeong Rok Yun; Manish Kumar Singh; Sunhee Han; Jyotsna S. Ranbhise; Hanjoon Seo; Sung Soo Kim; Insu...
abstract: Skeletal muscle plasticity is modulated by a delicate equilibrium between reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated signaling and oxidative distress. Although excessive oxidant accumulation impairs excit

title: Vitamin C and E antioxidant supplementation may significantly reduce pain symptoms in endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Patrick Bayu *, Jacobus Jeno Wibisono
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the efficacy of vitamin C and E supplementation for endometriosis pain. The findings suggest that this antioxidant combination significantly reduces chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhea, and dyspareunia compared to placebo.

title: Endogenous and Exogenous Antioxidants in Skeletal Muscle Fatigue Development during Exercise
authors: Elżbieta Supruniuk, Jan Górski, Adrian Chabowski
abstract: This paper reviews the dual role of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species in skeletal muscle fatigue during exercise. It concludes that both exercise-induced and antioxidant-supplemented ROS/RNS levels can impact muscle function by influencing signaling pathways and redox balance.

title: Radioiodine-induced oxidative stress in patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma and effect of supplementation with vitamins C and E and selenium (antioxidants)
authors: Pedro Weslley Rosário, Kelly Cristina Siqueira Batista, Maria Regina Calsolari
abstract: Radioiodine therapy for thyroid cancer was studied for its oxidative stress effects. Antioxidant supplementation significantly reduced this stress.

title: Vitamin C‐Dependent Intergenerational Inheritance of Enhanced Endurance Performance Following Maternal Exercise
authors: Haiwang Shi, Jie Li, Fan Li, Haoyang Yu, Fulong Zhang, Tao Wu, Luodan Yang, Yuecheng Li, Rui Hu, Men...
abstract: Maternal exercise enhances offspring endurance through muscle and mitochondrial changes, with benefits inherited across generations. This effect is mediated by vitamin C's role in regulating DNA methylation via the TET2-SVCT2 pathway.

title: The Effect of Combined Vitamin C and Vitamin E Supplementation on Oxidative Stress Markers in Women with Endometriosis: A Randomized, Triple-Blind Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Leila Amini, Razieh Chekini, Mohammad Reza Nateghi, Hamid Haghani, Tannaz Jamialahmadi, Thozhukat Sa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C and E supplementation on oxidative stress and pain in women with endometriosis. The supplementation significantly reduced oxidative stress markers and pelvic pain symptoms.

title: Does quercetin and vitamin C improve exercise performance, muscle damage, and body composition in male athletes?
authors: Gholamreza Askari, Reza Ghiasvand, Jahangir Karimian, Awat Feizi, Zamzam Paknahad, Gholamreza Sharif...
source: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences : The Official Journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated the effects of quercetin and vitamin C supplementation on male athletes' exercise performance, muscle damage, and body composition. The supplementation did not improve exercise performance but reduced muscle damage and body fat percentage.

title: Oxidant Antioxidants and Adaptive Responses to Exercise
authors: Paola Venditti, Mari Carmen Gomez-Cabrera, Yong Zhang, Zsolt Radak

title: Potential Vitamin E Signaling Mediators in Skeletal Muscle
authors: Elisabetta Meacci, Antony Chirco, Mercedes Garcia-Gil
abstract: This review examines Vitamin E's role in skeletal muscle and potential signaling mediators. It discusses bioactive sphingolipids and myokines as effectors and the benefits of Vitamin E supplementation for muscle health.

title: How N-Acetylcysteine Supplementation Affects Redox Regulation, Especially at Mitohormesis and Sarcohormesis Level: Current Perspective
authors: Aslı Devrim-Lanpir, Lee Hill, Beat Knechtle
abstract: This review examines N-acetylcysteine's effects on exercise-induced oxidative stress and athletic adaptation. It specifically focuses on how NAC influences mitohormesis and sarcohormesis.

title: Redox Mechanism of Reactive Oxygen Species in Exercise
authors: Feng He, Juan Li, Zewen Liu, Chia-Chen Chuang, Wenge Yang, Li Zuo
abstract: This review examines reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and antioxidant defenses during various exercise types. Moderate ROS exposure is crucial for adaptive responses, while excessive ROS can cause damage.

title: Effects of Quercetin and Citrulline on Nitric Oxide Metabolites and Antioxidant Biomarkers in Trained Cyclists
authors: Jennifer A. Kurtz, Rafaela G. Feresin, Jacob Grazer, Jeff Otis, Kathryn E. Wilson, J. Andrew Doyle, ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of quercetin and citrulline supplementation on nitric oxide and antioxidant biomarkers in trained cyclists. Neither combined nor independent supplementation significantly improved these biomarkers, suggesting limited ergogenic efficacy in this context.

title: Supplementation of Underfed Twin-Bearing Ewes with Herbal Vitamins C and E: Impacts on Birth Weight, Postnatal Growth, and Pre-Weaning Survival of the Lambs
authors: Víctor H. Parraguez, Francisco Sales, Oscar A. Peralta, Eileen Narbona, Raúl Lira, Mónica De los Rey...
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: Herbal vitamins C and E, alone or with concentrate, were supplemented to underfed twin-bearing ewes. Supplementation improved lamb birth weight and antioxidant capacity, with combined treatment showing the best results.

title: Resistance-Trained Individuals Are Less Susceptible to Oxidative Damage after Eccentric Exercise
authors: Ypatios Spanidis, Dimitrios Stagos, Christina Papanikolaou, Konstantina Karatza, Andria Theodosi, Ar...
abstract: Resistance-trained individuals experienced less oxidative damage and had a stronger antioxidant profile after eccentric exercise compared to untrained individuals. This suggests training status significantly influences exercise-induced oxidative stress and recovery.

title: Complex Effects of Vitamin E and Vitamin C Supplementation on  in Vitro  Neonatal Mononuclear Cell Responses to Allergens
authors: Heather J. H. Wassall, Graham Devereux, Anthony Seaton, Robert N. Barker
abstract: This study examined how vitamin E and C supplementation affects neonatal immune cells' response to allergens. Vitamin E showed complex effects, sometimes reducing proliferation and other times increasing it, while vitamin C had varied impacts on cytokine production.

title: Effects of Vitamin E and Zinc Supplementation on Antioxidants in Beta thalassemia major Patients
authors: Mohammadreza Rashidi, Maryam Aboomardani, Maryam Rafraf, Seyed-Rafie Arefhosseini, Abbasali Keshtkar...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and zinc supplementation on antioxidant levels in beta-thalassemia major patients. Supplementation with vitamin E and/or zinc increased serum levels of these nutrients and BMI, but decreased glutathione peroxidase activity.

title: Well-Trained Elders Have Antioxidant Responses and an Equal Magnitude of EIMD as Young Adults
authors: Eva Tékus, Nikolett Lilla Szénási, Edina Szabó, Zoltan Heckel, Tibor Mintál, Tamas Kőszegi, Tamas At...
abstract: This study examined antioxidant responses and muscle damage markers in young and older men after eccentric training. No significant differences in antioxidant capacity or muscle damage were found between the groups, suggesting similar adaptability.

title: Additional Effects of Nutritional Antioxidant Supplementation on Peripheral Muscle during Pulmonary Rehabilitation in COPD Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Fares Gouzi, Jonathan Maury, Nelly Héraud, Nicolas Molinari, Héléna Bertet, Bronia Ayoub, Marine Bla...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of antioxidant supplementation during pulmonary rehabilitation in COPD patients. Supplementation did not improve muscle endurance but enhanced muscle strength and reduced muscle weakness.

title: Effect of six weeks 1000 mg/day vitamin C supplementation and healthy training in elderly women on genes expression associated with the immune response - a randomized controlled trial
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Mariusz Zasada, Anna Piotrowska, Danuta Dworakowska, Olga C...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin C supplementation and exercise on immune gene expression in elderly women. While most genes showed no significant change, vitamin C supplementation showed a tendency to alter IL-6 and IL-10 expression.

title: The Antioxidant Role of Glutathione and N-Acetyl-Cysteine Supplements and Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress
authors: Chad Kerksick, Darryn Willoughby
abstract: This paper examines the antioxidant roles of glutathione and N-acetyl-cysteine supplements in mitigating exercise-induced oxidative stress. These antioxidants may help maintain cellular function and DNA integrity by reducing oxidative damage.

title: Comparison of the effects of two antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes
authors: Claudia D. Schneider, Patricia M. Bock, Georgia F. Becker, Jose Claudio F. Moreira, Adriane Bello-Kl...
abstract: This study compared the effects of regular and high antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes. A high antioxidant diet improved several markers of redox status in the athletes.

title: Effect of exercise and antioxidant supplementation on cellular lipid peroxidation in elderly individuals: Systematic review and network meta-analysis
authors: Chunxia Ni, Yiyi Ji, Keke Hu, Kai Xing, Yining Xu, Yanan Gao
abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined exercise and antioxidant supplementation's effects on cellular lipid peroxidation in the elderly. A combination of aerobic and resistance exercise with placebo intake most effectively reduced lipid peroxidation.

title: Tribbles 3 blunts exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation
authors: Ran Hee Choi, Abigail McConahay, Mackenzie B. Johnson, Morgan Ojemuyiwa, Brooklyn J. Phillips, Ha-Wo...
abstract: This study investigated the role of Tribbles 3 (TRB3) in exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation. TRB3 overexpression blunts exercise benefits, impairing glucose tolerance and metabolic gene expression, while TRB3 knockout improves glucose tolerance.

title: Low-Frequency Fatigue as an Indicator of Eccentric Exercise-Induced Muscle Injury: The Role of Vitamin E
authors: Antonios Kyparos, Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Konstantina Dipla, Andreas Zafeiridis, Vassilis Paschalis,...
abstract: This study examined if vitamin E reduces eccentric exercise-induced muscle injury in rats, using low-frequency fatigue as an indicator. Vitamin E supplementation improved muscle force decline and recovery, suggesting it attenuates exercise-induced injury.

title: Effect of Eicosapentaenoic Acid (EPA) and Vitamin E on the Blood Levels of Inflammatory Markers, Antioxidant Enzymes, and Lipid Peroxidation in Iranian Basketball Players
authors: R Ghiasvand, M Djalali, SA Djazayery, SA Keshavarz, M Hosseini, Gh Askari, N Jani, N Fardad, F Fateh...
abstract: This study examined the effects of EPA and vitamin E supplementation on inflammatory markers and antioxidant enzymes in basketball players. EPA with vitamin E reduced TNF-α and increased glutathione reductase, while EPA alone increased MDA.

title: Redox correlation in muscle lengthening and immune response in eccentric exercise
authors: Feng He, Chia-Chen Chuang, Tingyang Zhou, Qing Jiang, Darlene A. Sedlock, Li Zuo
abstract: Eccentric exercise in mice and humans was studied for its effects on muscle function and immune cells. Antioxidant supplementation attenuated exercise-induced changes in anti-apoptotic proteins and may protect against muscle dysfunction.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Vitamin Supplementation on Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Yizhou Ye, Jing Li, Zhongxiang Yuan
abstract: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials examined antioxidant vitamin supplementation's effect on cardiovascular outcomes. The study found no significant impact on major cardiovascular events, myocardial infarction, stroke, or death.

title: High-Dose Astaxanthin Supplementation Suppresses Antioxidant Enzyme Activity during Moderate-Intensity Swimming Training in Mice
authors: Yingsong Zhou, Julien S Baker, Xiaoping Chen, Yajun Wang, Haimin Chen, Gareth W Davison, Xiaojun Yan
abstract: High-dose astaxanthin supplementation was administered to mice undergoing swimming training. This supplementation suppressed antioxidant enzyme activity and downregulated Nrf2 signaling.

title: A metabolomic investigation of the effects of vitamin E supplementation in humans
authors: Max Wong, John K Lodge
abstract: This study investigated plasma metabolome changes after vitamin E supplementation in healthy males. Vitamin E supplementation altered lysophosphatidylcholine levels, suggesting an influence on phospholipid metabolism.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on NET Formation Induced by LPS In Vitro; the Roles of Vitamins E and C, Glutathione, and N-acetyl Cysteine
authors: Germán Muñoz-Sánchez, Lucila A. Godínez-Méndez, Mary Fafutis-Morris, Vidal Delgado-Rizo
abstract: This study investigated how antioxidant supplementation affects LPS-induced NET formation in neutrophils. Antioxidant combinations significantly reduced NET formation and oxidative stress markers in vitro.

title: Food-Based Antioxidant Nutrition for Exercise Recovery and Training Adaptation: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework for Redox Signaling, Dietary Matrices, and Periodized Application
authors: Hua Yang; Jingmei Dong; Jing Yang; Chieh-Chen Wu; Chun-Hsien Su
abstract: Exercise-induced reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) serve as crucial signaling molecules for training adaptation, mitochondrial biogenesis, and inflammatory resolution, rather than being mere

title: Dietary nanocomposite of vitamin C and vitamin E enhanced the performance of  Nile tilapia
authors: Ahmed H. Sherif, Riad H. Khalil, Talaat S. Talaat, Mohamed Z. Baromh, Mahmoud A. Elnagar
abstract: A nanocomposite of vitamins C and E was fed to Nile tilapia. This dietary nanocomposite significantly improved fish growth, immunity, and antioxidant levels, with the combined VCE-nanoparticle form showing the greatest benefits.

title: Effects of Resistance Training Combined with Vitamin D Supplementation on Health-Related Variables in the Elderly: Muscle Strength, Body Composition, and Inflammatory Status
authors: Lorena Cristina Ribeiro da Rosa, Paulo de Tarso Veras Farinatti, Maria Izabel Ferreira Batista, Hile...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study examined the effects of resistance training plus vitamin D supplementation on older adults. The combination did not improve strength, body composition, or inflammation more than resistance training alone.

title: Update: Is exercise-induced oxidative stress a friend or foe?
authors: Scott K. Powers; Mari Carmen Gomez-Cabrera
abstract: Exercise increases reactive oxygen species (ROS), which can cause oxidative damage. However, these ROS also act as signaling molecules, promoting beneficial exercise adaptations like increased mitochondria and antioxidant capacity. The net effect of exercise-induced ROS is a balance between damage and adaptive signaling.

title: The Effects of a Multiflavonoid Supplement on Vascular and Hemodynamic Parameters following Acute Exercise
authors: Rebecca M. Kappus, Chelsea D. Curry, Steve McAnulty, Janice Welsh, David Morris, David C. Nieman, Je...
abstract: A study investigated the effects of a multiflavonoid supplement on vascular and hemodynamic parameters during postexercise hypotension. The supplement enhanced postexercise blood pressure reduction and improved vascular distensibility compared to placebo.

title: Marginal vitamin C status is associated with reduced fat oxidation during submaximal exercise in young adults
authors: Carol S Johnston, Corinne Corte, Pamela D Swan
abstract: Marginal vitamin C status was studied in relation to fat oxidation during submaximal exercise. Low vitamin C status was associated with reduced fat oxidation, which was improved by vitamin C repletion.

title: Vitamin C may alleviate exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a meta-analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: This meta-analysis examined if vitamin C affects exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. Vitamin C administration significantly reduced post-exercise FEV1 decline and the proportion of participants experiencing EIB.

title: Reactive oxygen species promote endurance exercise-induced adaptations in skeletal muscles
authors: Scott K. Powers, Zsolt Radak, Li Li Ji, Malcolm Jackson
abstract: Contracting skeletal muscles produce reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly hydrogen peroxide, which are essential for exercise-induced adaptations. These ROS activate signaling pathways that promote mitochondrial biogenesis and the expression of key muscle proteins.

title: Exercise Training Combined with  Bifidobacterium Longum  OLP-01 Supplementation Improves Exercise Physiological Adaption and Performance
authors: Wen-Ching Huang, Yi-Ju Hsu, Chi-Chang Huang, Hsuan-Chen Liu, Mon-Chien Lee
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise training combined with *Bifidobacterium longum* OLP-01 supplementation in mice. The combination significantly improved exercise performance, reduced fatigue markers, and ameliorated exercise-induced inflammation and injury.

title: Combined high-intensity interval training and green tea supplementation enhance metabolic and antioxidant status in response to acute exercise in overweight women
authors: Elham Ghasemi, Mohammad Esmaeil Afzalpour, Shila Nayebifar
abstract: High-intensity interval training combined with green tea supplementation was studied in overweight women. This combination significantly improved metabolic and antioxidant status compared to training or supplementation alone.

title: Can Antioxidants Protect Against Disuse Muscle Atrophy?
authors: Scott K. Powers
abstract: This review examines the role of radicals in disuse muscle atrophy and analyzes literature on antioxidant effects. Evidence suggests specific antioxidants may help delay muscle loss due to inactivity.

title: Pterostilbene Enhances Endurance Capacity via Promoting Skeletal Muscle Adaptations to Exercise Training in Rats
authors: Jiawei Zheng, Wujian Liu, Xiaohui Zhu, Li Ran, Hedong Lang, Long Yi, Mantian Mi, Jundong Zhu
abstract: Pterostilbene (PST) was studied for its effects on skeletal muscle adaptations to exercise training in rats. PST supplementation enhanced exercise-induced improvements in endurance capacity by promoting slow-twitch fiber formation, angiogenesis, and mitochondrial biogenesis.

title: The effect of vitamin C on bronchoconstriction and respiratory symptoms caused by exercise: a review and statistical analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: Vitamin C was studied for its effects on exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and respiratory symptoms. It significantly reduced post-exercise lung function decline and the incidence of respiratory symptoms.

title: Nutritional Supplements to Support Resistance Exercise in Countering the Sarcopenia of Aging
authors: James McKendry, Brad S. Currier, Changhyun Lim, Jonathan C. Mcleod, Aaron C.Q. Thomas, Stuart M. Phi...
abstract: This review examines nutritional strategies to enhance resistance training for combating age-related muscle loss. Combining resistance exercise with specific nutrients and supplements can optimize muscle growth and maintenance, supporting healthspan in older adults.

title: Effect of endurance training and cinnamon supplementation on post-exercise oxidative responses in rats
authors: Gholamreza Dehghan, Mehrnoosh Shaghaghi, Afshar Jafari, Mustafa Mohammadi, Reza Badalzadeh
abstract: This study investigated the effects of endurance training and cinnamon supplementation on oxidative stress in rats after exhaustive exercise. The findings indicate that combining training and cinnamon supplementation offers the greatest protection against exercise-induced oxidative damage.

title: Individualised Exercise Training Enhances Antioxidant Buffering Capacity in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
authors: Tim J. M. Wallis, Magdalena Minnion, Anna Freeman, Andrew Bates, James M. Otto, Stephen A. Wootton, ...
abstract: An 8-week individualized exercise program was studied in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. The program improved exercise capacity and antioxidant buffering capacity, suggesting a potential mechanism for exercise benefits.

title: Repeated Supramaximal Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress: Effect of β-Alanine Plus Creatine Supplementation
authors: Muaz Belviranli, Nilsel Okudan, Serkan Revan, Serdar Balci, Hakki Gokbel
abstract: This study examined the impact of beta-alanine and creatine supplementation on oxidative stress markers during repeated high-intensity exercise. Beta-alanine supplementation showed a limited antioxidant effect, with some improvements in glutathione levels and total antioxidant capacity observed.

title: The interaction effects of aerobic exercise training and vitamin D supplementation on plasma lipid profiles and insulin resistance in ovariectomized rats
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Rastegar Hoseini
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of aerobic exercise and vitamin D on ovariectomized rats. The combination significantly improved lipid profiles and reduced insulin resistance.

title: Effect of carbohydrate–protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations
authors: Abdullah F. Alghannam, Iain Templeman, Joel E. Thomas, Dawid Jedrzejewski, Samuel Griffiths, Joseph ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of post-exercise carbohydrate-protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations in men and women. Post-exercise protein supplementation increased mTOR gene expression, but did not enhance improvements in maximal oxygen uptake compared to carbohydrate-only supplementation.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation Delays Cellular Senescence  In Vitro
authors: Giorgio La Fata, Nicole Seifert, Peter Weber, M. Hasan Mohajeri
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on cellular senescence in human cells. Vitamin E supplementation reduced senescent cells by downregulating P21 expression.

title: Impact of Polyphenol Antioxidants on Cycling Performance and Cardiovascular Function
authors: Joel D. Trinity, Matthew D. Pahnke, Justin R. Trombold, Edward F. Coyle
abstract: Polyphenol antioxidants were supplemented to endurance athletes for 7 days, followed by exercise testing in the heat. Supplementation did not improve cycling performance or alter cardiovascular and thermoregulatory responses.

title: Impact of Polyphenol Supplementation on Acute and Chronic Response to Resistance Training
authors: Kyle S. Beyer, Jeffrey R. Stout, David H. Fukuda, Adam R. Jajtner, Jeremy R. Townsend, David D. Chur...
source: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
abstract: This study examined polyphenol blend supplementation's effects on resistance training adaptations. Supplementation increased antioxidant capacity but did not alter strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Supplementation of L-Arginine, L-Glutamine, Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Folic Acid, and Green Tea Extract Enhances Serum Nitric Oxide Content and Antifatigue Activity in Mice
authors: Yi-Ming Chen, Huashuai Li, Yen-Shuo Chiu, Chi-Chang Huang, Wen-Chyuan Chen
abstract: A combined extract of L-arginine, L-glutamine, vitamins C and E, folic acid, and green tea extract was administered to mice. This supplementation increased nitric oxide content and improved exercise performance, suggesting an antifatigue effect.

title: Effects of protein supplementation on body composition, physiological adaptations, and performance during endurance training: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Yang Xiao, ZhengWu Deng, Wei Sun, JiaYi Li, WeiFeng Gao
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined protein supplementation's effects during endurance training. Protein supplementation modestly improved time to exhaustion and lean body mass, with potential VO2max benefits for untrained individuals.

title: Vitamin D3 supplementation enhances the effect of aerobic water-based training on physical fitness indices in obese and overweight menopausal women: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Foroozandeh Zaravar, Golamhossein Tamaddon, Mohammadamin Safari, Leila Zaravar, Maryam Koushkie Jahr...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of water-based aerobic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on overweight/obese postmenopausal women. Combining both interventions significantly improved BMI, handgrip strength, and gait speed more than either alone.

title: Comparative effects of vitamin D and vitamin C supplementations with and without endurance physical activity on metabolic syndrome patients: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Halgord Ali M. Farag, Mohammad Javad Hosseinzadeh-Attar, Belal A. Muhammad, Ahmad Esmaillzadeh, Abde...
abstract: This study compared vitamin D and C supplementation with and without exercise in metabolic syndrome patients. Combining supplements with exercise maximized benefits, particularly for vitamin D regarding glucose, cholesterol, and blood pressure.

title: Resistance Exercise Associated with Camu-Camu ( Myrciaria dubia ) and Creatine Supplementation Modulates Antioxidant Response and Cardiac Parameters in Wistar Rats
authors: Thaís Cupertino Fialho, Lívia Carvalho Sette Abrantes, Karina Vitória Cipriana Martins, Renner Phili...
abstract: Resistance exercise combined with camu-camu and creatine supplementation was studied in rats. This combination improved antioxidant capacity, enzyme activity, and cardiac muscle fiber size.

title: Impact of exercise training and supplemental oxygen on submaximal exercise performance in patients with COPD
authors: Daniel Neunhäuserer, Bernhard Reich, Barbara Mayr, Bernhard Kaiser, Bernd Lamprecht, David Niedersee...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with and without supplemental oxygen on COPD patients' submaximal exercise performance. Exercise training improved exercise tolerance and capacity, with supplemental oxygen having minimal additional benefits.

title: Diclofenac Administration after Physical Training Blunts Adaptations of Peripheral Systems and Leads to Losses in Exercise Performance: In Vivo and In Silico Analyses
authors: Rômulo Pillon Barcelos, Frederico Diniz Lima, Aline Alves Courtes, Ingrid Kich da Silva, Jose Eduard...
abstract: This study investigated diclofenac's impact on exercise adaptations in rats. Diclofenac blunted exercise-induced performance gains and tissue adaptations, despite reducing inflammation.

title: Editorial: Exercise-induced oxidative stress and the role of antioxidants in sport and exercise
authors: Hannah J. Moir, Marcin Maciejczyk, Mateusz Maciejczyk, Felipe J. Aidar, Hamid Arazi
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Housing temperature influences exercise training adaptations in mice
authors: Steffen H. Raun, Carlos Henriquez-Olguín, Iuliia Karavaeva, Mona Ali, Lisbeth L. V. Møller, Witold K...
abstract: This study investigated how housing temperature affects exercise training adaptations in mice. Thermoneutral housing reduced exercise-induced improvements in insulin action, energy expenditure, and body composition, indicating training adaptations are temperature-dependent.

title: Synergistic Role of Aerobic Exercise and Vitamin C in Reducing Hypertension and Restoring Redox–Inflammatory Balance
authors: Sheraz Ahmad, Khalid Abdul Majeed, Saima Masood, Muhammad Shahbaz Yousaf, Muhammad Bilal Akram, Abdu...
abstract: Aerobic exercise and vitamin C were studied for their effects on hypertension in rats. Combined intervention most effectively lowered blood pressure and improved hypertension-related changes.

title: Lower vascular conductance responses to handgrip exercise are improved following acute antioxidant supplementation in young individuals with post‐traumatic stress disorder
authors: Jennifer B. Weggen, Ashley M. Darling, Aaron S. Autler, Austin C. Hogwood, Kevin P. Decker, Jacob Ri...
abstract: This study examined vascular responses to handgrip exercise in young individuals with PTSD. Antioxidant supplementation improved vascular conductance during exercise in the PTSD group.

title: Nordic Walking Training Causes a Decrease in Blood Cholesterol in Elderly Women Supplemented with Vitamin D
authors: Krzysztof Prusik, Jakub Kortas, Katarzyna Prusik, Jan Mieszkowski, Joanna Jaworska, Wojciech Skrobot...
abstract: Nordic Walking training combined with vitamin D supplementation was studied in elderly women. This intervention significantly decreased total cholesterol, LDL-C, and triglycerides.

title: Haptoglobin Phenotype, Preeclampsia Risk and the Efficacy of Vitamin C and E Supplementation to Prevent Preeclampsia in a Racially Diverse Population
authors: Tracey L. Weissgerber, Robin E. Gandley, Paula L. McGee, Catherine Y. Spong, Leslie Myatt, Kenneth J...
abstract: This study investigated haptoglobin phenotype, preeclampsia risk, and vitamin supplementation efficacy. No association was found between haptoglobin phenotype and preeclampsia risk or vitamin efficacy, except for increased risk in Hispanic Hp 2-2 women.

title: Effects of a combined protein and antioxidant supplement on recovery of muscle function and soreness following eccentric exercise
authors: Stephen J. Ives, Samuel Bloom, Alexs Matias, Noelle Morrow, Natalya Martins, Yookee Roh, Daniel Eben...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined protein and antioxidant supplementation on muscle recovery after eccentric exercise. The combined supplement improved muscle soreness more than protein or carbohydrate alone.

title: Antioxidant Vitamin C Prevents Decline in Endothelial Function during Sitting
authors: Saurabh S. Thosar, Sylvanna L. Bielko, Chad S. Wiggins, James E. Klaunig, Kieren J. Mather, Janet P....
abstract: This study investigated if Vitamin C prevents endothelial function decline during prolonged sitting. Vitamin C supplementation prevented the impairment of femoral artery dilation after three hours of sitting.

title: Long-term quercetin supplementation reduces lipid peroxidation but does not improve performance in endurance runners
authors: Shane D Scholten, Igor N Sergeev
source: Open Access Journal of Sports Medicine
abstract: Quercetin supplementation was studied in endurance runners for six weeks. It reduced lipid peroxidation but did not improve running performance.

title: Vitamin D Supplementation Has No Impact on Cardiorespiratory Fitness, but Improves Inflammatory Status in Vitamin D Deficient Young Men Engaged in Resistance Training
authors: Lauri Savolainen, Saima Timpmann, Martin Mooses, Luule Medijainen, Lisette Tõnutare, Frederik Ross, ...
abstract: Vitamin D supplementation was studied in deficient young men undergoing resistance training. It improved inflammatory status but did not affect cardiorespiratory fitness.

title: Effects of Vitamin E Intake and Voluntary Wheel Running on Whole-Body and Skeletal Muscle Metabolism in Ovariectomized Mice
