authors: Youngyun Jin, Hee-Jung Yoon, Ki-Woong Park, Hanall Lee, Yuan Tan, Byung-Jun Ryu, Seung-Min Lee, Chae...
abstract: This study examined vitamin E intake and exercise effects on ovariectomized mice. Vitamin E improved skeletal muscle mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative stress, independent of exercise.

title: Supplemental Oxygen during Exercise Training in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
authors: SARA FAGGIAN, FRANCESCA BATTISTA, MARCO VECCHIATO, RICHARD CASABURI, MARGARETA EMTNER, NICOLA BORASI...
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: This review examines supplemental oxygen's role in COPD exercise training. Supplemental oxygen may benefit specific patients and conditions, particularly with high-intensity training, to enhance exercise tolerance and adaptations.

title: Effects of low-volume walking programme and vitamin E supplementation on oxidative damage and health-related variables in healthy older adults
authors: Jong-Hwan Park, Masashi Miyashita, Masaki Takahashi, Noriaki Kawanishi, Seong-Ryu Bae, Hyun-Shik Kim...
abstract: A low-volume walking program and vitamin E supplementation were studied in older adults. Both interventions, individually or combined, reduced oxidative damage markers.

title: Mitochondria-targeted antioxidant supplementation improves 8 km time trial performance in middle-aged trained male cyclists
authors: S. C. Broome, A. J. Braakhuis, C. J. Mitchell, T. L. Merry
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effect of MitoQ supplementation on cycling performance in trained male cyclists. MitoQ supplementation improved 8km time trial performance and increased average power output.

title: Effect of vitamin C and vitamin E on lung contusion: A randomized clinical trial study
authors: Davoodabadi Abdoulhossein, Iman Taheri, Mohammad ali Saba, Hossein Akbari, Shima Shafagh, Asemi Zata...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamins C and E on lung contusion patients. Co-administration of these vitamins improved arterial blood gas parameters and reduced ICU stay.

title: Mitochondria-Targeted Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Function
authors: Sophie C. Broome, Jonathan S. T. Woodhead, Troy L. Merry
abstract: This review summarizes literature on mitochondria-targeted antioxidants and skeletal muscle function. These antioxidants show benefits for muscle capacity, insulin sensitivity, and age-related decline, but effects depend on the specific antioxidant used.

title: Potential Benefits of Nitrate Supplementation on Antioxidant Defense System and Blood Pressure Responses after Exercise Performance
authors: Eduardo F. Menezes, Leonardo G. Peixoto, Renata R. Teixeira, Allisson B. Justino, Guilherme M. Puga,...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of sodium nitrate supplementation on oxidative stress and blood pressure after aerobic exercise. Five-day nitrate supplementation reduced systolic blood pressure and improved antioxidant capacity in healthy young men.

title: The effect of probiotic supplementation combined with aerobic exercise on the antioxidant capacity of college students
authors: Tong Wu, Yingfeng Chen, Kai Zhao, Chenzhe Liu, Wei Jiang
abstract: This study investigated the effects of probiotic supplementation and aerobic exercise on college students' antioxidant capacity. Combining probiotics with aerobic exercise significantly improved antioxidant capacity and reduced oxidative stress markers after high-intensity exercise.

title: Effects of acute and 14-day coenzyme Q10 supplementation on exercise performance in both trained and untrained individuals
authors: Matthew Cooke, Mike Iosia, Thomas Buford, Brian Shelmadine, Geoffrey Hudson, Chad Kerksick, Christop...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of acute and 14-day CoQ10 supplementation on exercise performance in trained and untrained individuals. CoQ10 supplementation increased plasma CoQ10 levels, but did not significantly improve exercise performance.

title: Physiological and Neural Adaptations to Eccentric Exercise: Mechanisms and Considerations for Training
authors: Nosratollah Hedayatpour, Deborah Falla
abstract: This review examines physiological and neural adaptations to eccentric exercise. It concludes that despite initial damage, eccentric exercise effectively stimulates muscle hypertrophy, increased cortical activity, and improved motor unit function for enhanced muscle performance.

title: Efficacy of vitamin and antioxidant supplements in prevention of cardiovascular disease: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
authors: Seung-Kwon Myung, Woong Ju, Belong Cho, Seung-Won Oh, Sang Min Park, Bon-Kwon Koo, Byung-Joo Park
abstract: This meta-analysis reviewed 50 randomized controlled trials on vitamin and antioxidant supplements for cardiovascular disease prevention. These supplements showed no overall benefit, with some minor risks and benefits disappearing in high-quality trials.

title: Effect of an 8-weeks aerobic training program in elderly on oxidative stress and Hsp72 expression in leukocytes during antioxidant supplementation
authors: David Simar; D. Malatesta; E. Mas; M. Delage; C. Caillaud
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: To investigate the effect of aerobic training in the context of antioxidant supplementation on systemic oxidative stress and leukocytes heat shock protein (Hsp)72 expression in the elderly. Sixteen se

title: The effect of endurance training with and without vitamin E on expression of p53 and PTEN tumor suppressing genes in prostate glands of male rats
authors: Amin Allah Dashtiyan, Masood Sepehrimanesh, Nader Tanideh, Mohammad Esmaeil Afzalpour
abstract: Endurance training was studied for its effect on prostate tumor suppressor genes in rats, with and without vitamin E. Endurance training reduced p53 expression, while vitamin E alone increased PTEN expression.

title: Vitamin E and Metabolic Health: Relevance of Interactions with Other Micronutrients
authors: Sijia Liao, Sylvia Oghogho Omage, Lisa Börmel, Stefan Kluge, Martin Schubert, Maria Wallert, Stefan ...
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's interactions with other micronutrients and their impact on metabolic health. These interactions may explain discrepancies in clinical trials and influence vitamin E's physiological functions.

title: Endurance Training Depletes Antioxidant System but Does Not Affect Endothelial Functions in Women with Abdominal Obesity: A Randomized Trial with a Comparison to Endurance-Strength Training
authors: Małgorzata Jamka, Paweł Bogdański, Patrycja Krzyżanowska-Jankowska, Anna Miśkiewicz-Chotnicka, Joann...
abstract: Endurance and endurance-strength training were compared in abdominally obese women. Endurance training depleted antioxidant systems but did not affect endothelial function, unlike endurance-strength training.

title: Astaxanthin-, β-Carotene-, and Resveratrol-Rich Foods Support Resistance Training-Induced Adaptation
authors: Aki Kawamura, Wataru Aoi, Ryo Abe, Yukiko Kobayashi, Masashi Kuwahata, Akane Higashi
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with nutrient-rich foods on muscle adaptation in men. Consuming foods rich in astaxanthin, β-carotene, and resveratrol enhanced strength and metabolic improvements from training.

title: Excessive Vitamin E Supplementation: Implications for Ovarian Physiology and Reproductive Health
authors: Farzaneh Rabiee, Masoud Fattahi, Mohammad Iranzad, Mohsen Rahimi Andani, Farnoosh Jafarpour, Mohamma...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different vitamin E doses on mouse reproductive health. Excessive vitamin E supplementation impaired fertility, oocyte and embryo development, and ovarian function by altering oxidative stress markers.

title: Cross-Sectional Associations Between Dietary Antioxidant Vitamins C, E and Carotenoid Intakes and Sarcopenic Indices in Women Aged 18–79 Years
authors: A. A. Welch, A. Jennings, E. Kelaiditi, J. Skinner, C. J. Steves
abstract: This study examined the relationship between dietary antioxidant vitamin intake and sarcopenic indices in women. Higher vitamin C and carotenoid intake was associated with greater skeletal muscle mass and power, especially in younger women.

title: The effects of exercise training and acute exercise duration on plasma folate and vitamin B 12
authors: Young-Nam Kim, Ji Hyeon Hwang, Youn-Ok Cho
abstract: This study examined how exercise training and acute exercise duration affect plasma folate and vitamin B12 in rats. Regular exercise training lowered folate and raised vitamin B12, but acute exercise duration had no significant impact on these vitamins.

title: Tissue-Specific Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Eugene Jansen, Dale Viezeliene, Piet Beekhof, Eric Gremmer, Leonid Ivanov
abstract: A study supplemented mice with varying vitamin E doses, including a high dose (25× RDI). High vitamin E intake showed beneficial effects in male mouse livers but caused toxicity and inflammation in male mouse kidneys.

title: Combined effects of green tea supplementation and eccentric exercise on nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 activity
authors: Josh Thorley, Craig Thomas, Nicolas Thon, Hannah Nuttall, Neil R. W. Martin, Nicolette Bishop, Steph...
abstract: This study examined the combined effects of green tea supplementation and eccentric exercise on NRF2 activity. Eccentric exercise, with or without green tea, did not significantly increase NRF2 activity.

title: The role of resistance training and creatine supplementation on oxidative stress, antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life in older adults
authors: Ehsan Amiri, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani
abstract: Resistance training with creatine supplementation was studied in older adults. This intervention improved antioxidant defense, muscle strength, and quality of life, with creatine enhancing strength gains.

title: Protective Role of Vitamin C Intake on Muscle Damage in Male Adolescents Performing Strenuous Physical Activity
authors: Shreef G. N. Gabrial, Marie-Christine R. Shakib, Gamal N. Gabrial
source: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's effect on muscle damage in male adolescents during strenuous exercise. Vitamin C supplementation significantly reduced markers of muscle damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: Combined Effects of Exercise Training and Nutritional Supplementation in Cancer Patients in the Context of the COVID-19: A Perspective Study
authors: Mahdieh Molanouri Shamsi, Alieh Vahed, AmirHossin Ahmadi Hekmatikar, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This perspective study examines how exercise and nutritional supplements might affect cancer patients' COVID-19 risk. Combining these interventions could boost immune responses against COVID-19 and potentially improve vaccine efficacy.

title: Mitigating the Growth, Biochemical Changes, Genotoxic and Pathological Effects of Copper Toxicity in Broiler Chickens by Supplementing Vitamins C and E
authors: Mohamed A. Hashem, Sahar S. Abd El Hamied, Eman M. A. Ahmed, Shimaa A. Amer, Mohamed E. El-Sharnouby
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: This study investigated the effects of copper sulfate toxicity and vitamin C/E supplementation on broiler chickens. Vitamins C and E, especially when combined, helped mitigate the negative impacts of copper toxicity on growth and liver health.

title: Impact of Vitamin D on Physical Efficiency and Exercise Performance—A Review
authors: Michał Wiciński, Dawid Adamkiewicz, Monika Adamkiewicz, Maciej Śniegocki, Marta Podhorecka, Paweł Sz...
abstract: This review examines vitamin D's impact on physical efficiency and exercise performance. Vitamin D influences muscle function, bone health, and immune response, potentially enhancing athletic capabilities.

title: Effects of creatine supplementation associated with resistance training on oxidative stress in different tissues of rats
authors: Giuseppe Potrick Stefani, Ramiro Barcos Nunes, André Zuanazzi Dornelles, Jadson Pereira Alves, Marce...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated creatine supplementation with resistance training on strength and oxidative stress in rats. Creatine, alone or with training, reduced oxidative stress and enhanced strength gain, acting as a non-enzymatic antioxidant.

title: Influence of Vitamin D Supplementation by Sunlight or Oral D3 on Exercise Performance
authors: ALEXANDER T. CARSWELL, SAMUEL J. OLIVER, LAUREL M. WENTZ, DANIEL S. KASHI, ROSS ROBERTS, JONATHAN C....
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: A prospective study found vitamin D status positively correlated with endurance, but not strength or power. Supplementing to achieve vitamin D sufficiency via sunlight or oral D3 did not improve exercise performance.

title: Vitamin E supplementation and pneumonia risk in males who initiated smoking at an early age: effect modification by body weight and dietary vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: This study examined vitamin E's effect on pneumonia risk in early-smoking males. Vitamin E increased pneumonia risk in underweight and very overweight smokers, especially those with high dietary vitamin C.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation and circuit training on indices of obesity and insulin resistance in T2D and vitamin D deficient elderly women
authors: Hyoung-Jun Kim, Chang-Kyun Kang, Hyon Park, Man-Gyoon Lee
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamin D and circuit training on obese, vitamin D-deficient elderly women with type 2 diabetes. Circuit training alone improved body composition, abdominal fat, and blood lipids, while combined treatment showed a trend toward improved insulin resistance.

title: The effects of endogenously‐ and exogenously‐induced hyperketonemia on exercise performance and adaptation
authors: David J. Dearlove, Adrian Soto Mota, David Hauton, Katherine Pinnick, Rhys Evans, Jack Miller, Roman...
abstract: This study compared exercise capacity and adaptation with carbohydrate-rich, ketone-supplemented, and ketogenic diets. Ketone supplementation improved exercise capacity, while a ketogenic diet impaired it and reduced insulin sensitivity.

title: The effect of aquatic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on bone metabolism in postmenopausal obese women
authors: Foroozandeh Zaravar, Gholamhossein Tamaddon, Leila Zaravar, Maryam Koushkie Jahromi
source: Journal of Exercise Science and Fitness
abstract: This study investigated the effects of aquatic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on bone metabolism in postmenopausal obese women. Combining both interventions was most effective for improving bone metabolism, while vitamin D alone was insufficient and aquatic training did not improve vitamin D levels.

title: Acute vitamin C improves cardiac function, not exercise capacity, in adults with type 2 diabetes
authors: Rebecca L. Scalzo, Timothy A. Bauer, Kylie Harrall, Kerrie Moreau, Cemal Ozemek, Leah Herlache, Shaw...
abstract: Acute vitamin C infusion was studied in adults with type 2 diabetes and healthy adults. Vitamin C improved diastolic cardiac function but did not affect exercise capacity or other measures of vascular function.

title: Marginal Ascorbate Status (Hypovitaminosis C) Results in an Attenuated Response to Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Juliet M. Pullar, Stephanie M. Bozonet, Margreet C. M. Vissers
abstract: This study analyzed vitamin C supplementation in individuals with low baseline levels. A 50 mg/day supplement was insufficient to restore adequate vitamin C status in these individuals.

title: The Role of Vitamin C in Two Distinct Physiological States: Physical Activity and Sleep
authors: Aneta Otocka-Kmiecik, Aleksandra Król
abstract: This paper reviews the relationship between vitamin C, physical activity, and sleep. Vitamin C supplementation may benefit sleep health and aspects of physical activity, potentially by influencing oxidative stress.

title: Proteome-Driven Elucidation of Adaptive Responses
authors: to Combined Vitamin E and C Deficiency in Zebrafish
abstract: This study investigated the proteomic changes in zebrafish due to combined vitamin E and C deficiency. Vitamin C deficiency, especially with vitamin E deficiency, induces stress responses and shifts cellular energy metabolism.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of a Period of Aerobic Training and Vitamin D Supplementation in Postmenopausal Women with Metabolic Syndrome
authors: Parivash Najafi Nazarabadi, Zaher Etemad, Rastegar Hoseini, Fatah Moradi
abstract: This study examined the anti-inflammatory effects of aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation in postmenopausal women with metabolic syndrome. The combination of exercise and vitamin D significantly reduced inflammatory markers and improved metabolic syndrome indices more than either intervention alone.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation combined with exercise on glucolipid metabolism in adults: A meta-analysis
authors: Yue Feng, Wenxing Zhou, Yanjun Niu
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of vitamin D and exercise combined on glucolipid metabolism. The combination significantly improved blood glucose, fasting insulin, and insulin resistance, and increased vitamin D levels.

title: Vitamin C and Cardiovascular Disease: An Update
authors: Marco B. Morelli, Jessica Gambardella, Vanessa Castellanos, Valentina Trimarco, Gaetano Santulli
abstract: This review assesses studies on vitamin C's role in cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. It discusses potential benefits, pitfalls, and controversies in this research area.

title: Effect of resistance training plus enriched probiotic supplement on sestrin2, oxidative stress, and mitophagy markers in elderly male Wistar rats
authors: Majid Mohabbat, Hamid Arazi
abstract: Resistance training with a probiotic supplement was studied in aged rats. This combination improved antioxidant capacity and mitophagy markers, suggesting it may help reduce age-related muscle strength loss.

title: Reexamination of a Meta-Analysis of the Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Mortality and Health in Randomized Trials
authors: Hans K. Biesalski, Tilman Grune, Jana Tinz, Iris Zöllner, Jeffrey B. Blumberg
abstract: This paper re-examines a meta-analysis on antioxidant supplementation. The re-evaluation found that most trials showed neutral or positive outcomes, suggesting benefits should be considered alongside risks.

title: Effects of Vitamin C Supplementation on Plasma and Urinary Vitamin C Concentration in Korean Women
authors: Jayoung Choi, Do-Yeon Kim, Ryowon Choue, Hyunjung Lim
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 100 mg and 2,000 mg vitamin C supplements on Korean women. Both doses increased plasma and urinary vitamin C, with the higher dose reducing oxidative stress and the lower dose reducing fatigue.

title: Effects of Methoxyisoflavone, Ecdysterone, and Sulfo-Polysaccharide Supplementation on Training Adaptations in Resistance-Trained Males
authors: Colin D Wilborn, Lemuel W Taylor, Bill I Campbell, Chad Kerksick, Chris J Rasmussen, Michael Greenwo...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Methoxyisoflavone, ecdysterone, and sulfo-polysaccharide were studied for their effects on resistance-trained males. Supplementation did not improve body composition, strength, or anabolic/catabolic markers.

title: The effects of multi mineral-vitamin D and vitamins (C+E) supplementation in the prevention of preeclampsia: An RCT
authors: Milad Azami, Tayebe Azadi, Sepidezahra Farhang, Shoobo Rahmati, Khadijeh Pourtaghi
abstract: A randomized trial investigated multimineral-vitamin D and vitamins C+E supplementation in pregnant women. Multimineral-vitamin D significantly reduced preeclampsia incidence and neonatal complications compared to controls.

title: Influence of training status on high-intensity intermittent performance in response to β-alanine supplementation
authors: Vitor de Salles Painelli, Bryan Saunders, Craig Sale, Roger Charles Harris, Marina Yázigi Solis, Ham...
abstract: This study examined the impact of β-alanine supplementation on high-intensity cycling performance in trained and non-trained individuals. β-alanine improved performance in both groups, demonstrating its effectiveness regardless of training status.

title: Vitamin E: Where Are We Now in Vascular Diseases?
authors: Anahita Garg, Jetty Chung-Yung Lee
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's role in vascular health, focusing on its antioxidant and regulatory effects. While its antioxidant benefits are known, its potential as a vascular regulatory molecule requires further study.

title: Effects of 12-weeks resistance training and vitamin E supplementation on aminotransferases, CTRP-2, and CTRP-9 levels in males with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: a double-blind, randomized trial
authors: Irfan Varmazyar, Amir Abbas Monazzami, Mozhgan Moradi, Andrew J McAinch
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: Resistance training and vitamin E supplementation were studied in males with NAFLD. Resistance training improved health markers, with vitamin E adding benefits only for aminotransferase levels.

title: The combination of exercise training and  Zataria multiflora  supplementation increase serum irisin levels in postmenopausal women
authors: Abbass Ghanbari-Niaki, Ayoub Saeidi, Mehdi Ahmadian, Leila Gharahcholo, Nooshin Naghavi, Mohammad Fa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise and *Zataria multiflora* supplementation on irisin levels in postmenopausal women. Combining exercise and supplementation significantly increased irisin compared to a control group.

title: White tea modulates antioxidant defense of endurance-trained rats
authors: Patrícia Berilli, Gustavo Bernardes Fanaro, Jéssica Piva Santos, Felix Guillermo Reyes Reyes, Amadeu...
abstract: White tea was given to endurance-trained rats to assess its impact on antioxidant defenses after exhaustive exercise. Long-term white tea consumption improved antioxidant capacity and reduced oxidative damage, suggesting a role in managing exercise-induced stress.

title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation and Exercise Training on Exercise Performance in Middle-Aged Mice
authors: Nai-Wen Kan, Chin-Shan Ho, Yen-Shuo Chiu, Wen-Ching Huang, Pei-Yu Chen, Yu-Tang Tung, Chi-Chang Huan...
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of resveratrol supplementation and exercise training on middle-aged mice. The combination significantly improved muscle strength and endurance compared to individual interventions.

title: Prevention of Teratogenesis in Pregnancies of Obese Rats by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Martin Alcala, Victoria E. Bolado, Isabel Sánchez-Vera, Sonia Clapés, Francisco Dasí, Guillermo Sáez...
abstract: Obese rats were supplemented with vitamin E to investigate its effect on teratogenesis. Vitamin E prevented malformations by maintaining maternal glutathione levels, which protected embryos from oxidative stress.

title: Effects of aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation on glycemic indices and adipose tissue gene expression in type 2 diabetic rats
authors: Kimya Khaledi, Rastegar Hoseini, Ahmad Gharzi
abstract: Aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation were studied in type 2 diabetic rats. Combined intervention significantly upregulated key genes in visceral adipose tissue compared to individual treatments.

title: Combined Effects of Spirulina Liquid Extract and Endurance Training on Aerobic Performance and Muscle Metabolism Adaptation in Wistar Rats
authors: Jordi Vignaud, Céline Loiseau, Martine Côme, Isabelle Martin, Rova Rasoanarivo, Josiane Hérault, Cla...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Spirulina liquid extract and endurance training on Wistar rats. Spirulina supplementation improved aerobic performance and muscle adaptation by enhancing antioxidant defenses and mitochondrial biogenesis.

title: Resistance Training Diminishes Mitochondrial Adaptations to Subsequent Endurance Training
authors: Paulo H. C. Mesquita, Joshua S. Godwin, Bradley A. Ruple, Casey L. Sexton, Mason C. McIntosh, Breann...
abstract: Resistance training followed by endurance training was studied in young adults. Prior resistance training diminished mitochondrial adaptations to subsequent endurance training.

title: The Impact of Exercise Training and Supplemental Oxygen on Peripheral Muscles in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: DANIEL NEUNHÄUSERER, MARTIN HUDELMAIER, DAVID NIEDERSEER, MARCO VECCHIATO, WOLFGANG WIRTH, EVA STEID...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise training with or without supplemental oxygen on peripheral muscles in COPD patients. Supplemental oxygen enhanced exercise training's impact on peak work rate and muscle cross-sectional area, suggesting it aids training adaptations.

title: Effects of Resistance Training on the Redox Status of Skeletal Muscle in Older Adults
authors: Paulo H. C. Mesquita, Donald A. Lamb, Joshua S. Godwin, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley A. Ruple, Johnatho...
abstract: Resistance training in older adults increased antioxidant enzyme activity and decreased oxidative damage in skeletal muscle. This suggests multi-level regulation of muscle redox status in response to training.

title: Effects of Rhodiola Rosea Supplementation on Exercise and Sport: A Systematic Review
authors: Yao Lu, Bin Deng, Luhua Xu, Hanjiao Liu, Yinzhi Song, Fengxia Lin
abstract: This systematic review evaluated Rhodiola rosea supplementation for exercise and sport. Most studies found it positively impacts athletic ability and performance with no significant adverse effects.

title: The Effects of Omega-3 Supplementation Combined with Strength Training on Neuro-Biomarkers, Inflammatory and Antioxidant Responses, and the Lipid Profile in Physically Healthy Adults
authors: Sedat Okut, Murat Ozan, Yusuf Buzdağli, Halil Uçar, Muhammet Raşit İnaç, Muhammet Talha Han, Esra Ba...
abstract: This study examined the effects of omega-3 supplementation alongside strength training in healthy adults. The combination significantly improved lipid profiles, reduced inflammation, enhanced antioxidant status, boosted neuro-biomarkers, and increased physical performance.

title: Effects of antioxidant supplementation on oxidative stress balance in young footballers- a randomized double-blind trial
authors: Błażej Stankiewicz, Mirosława Cieślicka, Sławomir Kujawski, Elżbieta Piskorska, Tomasz Kowalik, Just...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Young footballers were given chokeberry juice for 7 weeks to study its effect on oxidative stress. The supplementation did not significantly alter oxidative stress markers, biochemical parameters, or performance.

title: Randomised Controlled Trial of Fish Oil Supplementation on Responsiveness to Resistance Exercise Training in Sarcopenic Older Women
authors: Natália Maira da Cruz Alves, Karina Pfrimer, Priscila Carvalho Santos, Ellen Cristini de Freitas, Th...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial examined fish oil's effect on resistance training in sarcopenic older women. Fish oil supplementation significantly enhanced muscle strength gains compared to placebo.

title: The Effects of Supplementation with a Vitamin and Mineral Complex with Guaraná Prior to Fasted Exercise on Affect, Exertion, Cognitive Performance, and Substrate Metabolism: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Rachel C. Veasey, Crystal F. Haskell-Ramsay, David O. Kennedy, Karl Wishart, Silvia Maggini, Caspar ...
abstract: A vitamin and mineral complex with guaraná was given to active males before fasted exercise. This supplementation reduced perceived exertion during exercise and improved subsequent memory performance.

title: Effects of Exercise Alone or Combined With Cognitive Training and Vitamin D Supplementation to Improve Cognition in Adults With Mild Cognitive Impairment
authors: Manuel Montero-Odasso, Guangyong Zou, Mark Speechley, Quincy J. Almeida, Teresa Liu-Ambrose, Laura E...
abstract: A 20-week multidomain intervention combining exercise and cognitive training improved cognition in adults with mild cognitive impairment. Adding vitamin D did not enhance these cognitive benefits.

title: Effect of Antioxidants Supplementation on Aging and Longevity
authors: Izabela Sadowska-Bartosz, Grzegorz Bartosz
abstract: This paper reviews studies on antioxidant supplementation in model organisms to test the free radical theory of aging. Findings suggest that antioxidant effects on lifespan are often indirect or unrelated to their antioxidant properties, questioning the legitimacy of human supplementation.

title: Effects of Dietary Vitamin C Supplementation on Vitamin C Synthesis, Transport, and Egg Deposition in Breeding Geese
authors: Yanglei Hu, Rong Xu, Yating Zhou, Ning Li, Haiming Yang, Jian Wang, Hongchang Zhao, Jun Yu
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: This study investigated the impact of dietary vitamin C on vitamin C levels and transport in breeding geese. Supplementation increased vitamin C in egg yolks and serum by enhancing intestinal absorption and yolk deposition, while suppressing synthesis.

title: Exercise May Ameliorate the Detrimental Side Effects of High Vitamin D Supplementation on Muscle Function in Mice
authors: Danielle A Debruin, Cara A Timpani, Hannah Lalunio, Emma Rybalka, Craig A Goodman, Alan Hayes
source: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research
abstract: High vitamin D supplementation reduced muscle force in sedentary mice. Exercise normalized this effect and improved fatigue resistance.

title: Protein and the Adaptive Response With Endurance Training: Wishful Thinking or a Competitive Edge?
authors: Pim Knuiman, Maria T. E. Hopman, Conor Verbruggen, Marco Mensink
abstract: This perspective reviews the current evidence on protein's role in endurance training adaptations. While acute exercise may increase amino acid oxidation, the impact of dietary protein on endurance performance remains largely unproven.

title: Ketone ester supplementation blunts overreaching symptoms during endurance training overload
authors: Chiel Poffé, Monique Ramaekers, Ruud Van Thienen, Peter Hespel
abstract: Ketone ester supplementation was studied in endurance athletes undergoing training overload. This supplementation blunted overreaching symptoms and enhanced performance.

title: Vitamin C Supplementation Slightly Improves Physical Activity Levels and Reduces Cold Incidence in Men with Marginal Vitamin C Status: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Carol S. Johnston, Gillean M. Barkyoumb, Sara S. Schumacher
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C supplementation's effects on physical activity and colds in men with marginal vitamin C status. Supplementation slightly increased physical activity and reduced cold incidence and duration.

title: Combined Effects of Phytochemicals and Exercise on Fatty Acid Oxidation
authors: Jong-Hee Kim, Yoonjung Park
abstract: This review examines how phytochemicals and exercise affect fatty acid oxidation. Certain phytochemicals combined with exercise can increase fatty acid oxidation without increasing total energy expenditure.

title: Aerobic training and vitamin E administration ameliorates cardiac apoptosis markers in rats exposed to methamphetamine
authors: Hamidreza Salimi, Amir Hossein Haghighi, Shima Ababzadeh, Hamid Marefati, Sadegh Abbasian, Amber L. ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of aerobic training and vitamin E on cardiac apoptosis markers in rats exposed to methamphetamine. Both aerobic training and vitamin E reduced markers of cardiac apoptosis induced by methamphetamine.

title: Serum Oxidant and Antioxidant Status in Adolescents Undergoing Professional Endurance Sports Training
authors: Tom K. Tong, Hua Lin, Giuseppe Lippi, Jinlei Nie, Ye Tian
abstract: This study examined serum oxidant and antioxidant levels in adolescent endurance athletes versus untrained individuals. Athletes showed increased antioxidant enzymes, suggesting adaptation to exercise helps maintain redox balance.

title: The Synergistic Effects of Resveratrol combined with Resistant Training on Exercise Performance and Physiological Adaption
authors: Nai-Wen Kan, Mon-Chien Lee, Yu-Tang Tung, Chien-Chao Chiu, Chi-Chang Huang, Wen-Ching Huang
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of resveratrol and resistance training on exercise performance and physiological adaptations in mice. The combination showed synergistic benefits for grip strength, anaerobic capacity, and lactate levels, suggesting potential for improved health and physical activity.

title: Vitamin C and Neutrophil Function: Findings from Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Mikee Liugan, Anitra C. Carr
abstract: This review systematically analyzed randomized controlled trials on vitamin C's effects on neutrophil function. Vitamin C supplementation showed positive effects on neutrophil migration, phagocytosis, oxidative burst, and apoptosis in various patient groups and healthy individuals.

title: Dietary Nitrate Supplementation and Exercise Performance
authors: Andrew M. Jones
abstract: This review examines how dietary nitrate supplementation affects exercise performance. Findings suggest nitrate can reduce exercise oxygen cost and improve performance by increasing nitric oxide availability.

title: L-arginine Supplementation Does Not Enhance Anaerobic Performance in Trained Female Handball Players
authors: Mozhgan Mardokhi, Mohammad Rahman Rahimi, Saber Saedmocheshi, Manuel Vasquez-Muñoz, David Cristobal ...
abstract: This study examined the effects of L-arginine supplementation combined with high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on female handball players. L-arginine supplementation did not enhance anaerobic performance beyond HIIT alone and may negatively impact agility.

title: 6-Week Supplementation with  Tribulus terrestris  L. to Trained Male CrossFit ®  Athletes on Muscle, Inflammation, and Antioxidant Biomarkers: A Randomized, Single-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Diego Fernández-Lázaro, Jesús Seco-Calvo, Jorge Pascual-Fernández, Carlos Domínguez-Ortega, Miguel D...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 6-week *Tribulus terrestris* supplementation on trained male CrossFit athletes. Supplementation attenuated oxidative stress, muscle damage, and inflammation compared to placebo.

title: Independent and Combined Effects of Antioxidant Supplementation and Circuit Resistance Training on Selected Adipokines in Postmenopausal Women
authors: Ayoub Saeidi, Georges Jabbour, Mehdi Ahmadian, Asieh Abbassi-Daloii, Fatemeh Malekian, Anthony C. Ha...
abstract: Circuit resistance training and Zataria Multiflora supplementation were studied in postmenopausal women. The combination of both interventions showed greater improvements in selected adipokines than either intervention alone.

title: Vitamin E in Sarcopenia: Current Evidences on Its Role in Prevention and Treatment
authors: Shy Cian Khor, Norwahidah Abdul Karim, Wan Zurinah Wan Ngah, Yasmin Anum Mohd Yusof, Suzana Makpol
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's potential role in preventing and treating sarcopenia, an age-related muscle loss syndrome. While promising antioxidant properties exist, current evidence for its direct impact on muscle health remains inconclusive.

title: The effects of exercise training and nutritional supplementation on taekwondo performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Chen Xu, Wenxin Zhang, Lin Luo
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the effects of exercise training and nutritional supplementation on taekwondo performance. Both interventions significantly improved agility, kick performance, and aerobic capacity, though results should be generalized cautiously.

title: Cardiovascular and Metabolic Protection by Vitamin E: A Matter of Treatment Strategy?
authors: Melanie Ziegler, Maria Wallert, Stefan Lorkowski, Karlheinz Peter
abstract: This paper reviews vitamin E's role in cardiovascular health, highlighting conflicting trial results. It concludes that acute vitamin E treatment, not chronic supplementation, may offer clinical benefits, particularly in acute conditions like myocardial infarction.

title: Laying performance, digestibility and plasma hormones in laying hens exposed to chronic heat stress as affected by betaine, vitamin C, and/or vitamin E supplementation
authors: Youssef A. Attia, Abd El-Hamid E. Abd El-Hamid, Ahmed A. Abedalla, Marfat A. Berika, Mohammed A. Al-...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of betaine, vitamin C, and vitamin E supplementation on laying hens under chronic heat stress. Vitamin C supplementation showed the greatest improvement in laying performance and combatted heat stress effects.

title: Efficacy of Vitamin D Supplementation in Addition to Aerobic Exercise Training in Obese Women with Perceived Myalgia: A Single-Blinded Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Heba Ahmed Ali Abdeen, David Rodriguez-Sanz, Mahmoud Ewidea, Dina Mohamed Ali Al-Hamaky, Marwa Abd E...
abstract: This study examined vitamin D and aerobic exercise for obese women with muscle pain. Combining both treatments was most effective for reducing pain, improving vitamin D levels, and enhancing quality of life.

title: Influence of combined vitamin D 3  supplementation and resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older men and women (EXVITD): protocol for a randomised controlled trial
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Welford, Susan Lanham-New, Janet Lord, Alison Doyle, Julie Robinson, Peter Nighting...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial investigates the effect of vitamin D3 supplementation combined with resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older adults. The study aims to determine if this combination improves muscle function more than exercise training alone.

title: Concurrent effects of high-intensity interval training and vitamin D supplementation on bone metabolism among women diagnosed with osteoporosis: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Ahmad H. Alghadir, Sami A. Gabr, Amir Iqbal
abstract: This study examined the effects of 16 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and vitamin D supplementation on bone metabolism in women with osteoporosis. Concurrent HIIT and vitamin D supplementation significantly improved bone mineral density and bone metabolism markers more than either intervention alone.

title: α -Tocopherol Protects the Heart, Muscles, and Testes from Lipid Peroxidation in Growing Male Rats Subjected to Physical Efforts
authors: Magdalena Górnicka, Anna Ciecierska, Jadwiga Hamulka, Małgorzata E. Drywień, Joanna Frackiewicz, Krz...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of training and α-tocopherol supplementation on tissue α-tocopherol and lipid peroxidation in male rats. Supplementation helped prevent exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in the heart, muscles, and testes.

title: Chronic CaMKII inhibition blunts the cardiac contractile response to exercise training
authors: Guri Kaurstad, Marcia N. Alves, Ole J. Kemi, Natale Rolim, Morten A. Høydal, Helene Wisløff, Tomas O...
abstract: Chronic CaMKII inhibition was studied in mice undergoing exercise training. This inhibition blunted the improvement in cardiac contractile function typically seen with exercise, despite a paradoxical increase in maximal oxygen uptake.

title: Rhodiola/Cordyceps -Based Herbal Supplement Promotes Endurance Training-Improved Body Composition But Not Oxidative Stress and Metabolic Biomarkers: A Preliminary Randomized Controlled Study
authors: Yi-Hung Liao, Yi-Chen Chao, Brenton Yim-Quan Sim, Hui-Mei Lin, Mu-Tsung Chen, Chung-Yu Chen
abstract: This study examined the effects of an 8-week endurance training program combined with a Rhodiola/Cordyceps supplement. The supplement enhanced improvements in body composition but did not affect oxidative stress or metabolic biomarkers compared to placebo.

title: Biomarkers of Antioxidant Status, Inflammation, and Cartilage Metabolism Are Affected by Acute Intense Exercise but Not Superoxide Dismutase Supplementation in Horses
authors: Emily D. Lamprecht, Carey A. Williams
abstract: Acute intense exercise in horses increased biomarkers of inflammation and cartilage metabolism, but not antioxidant status. Superoxide dismutase supplementation did not alter these responses.

title: Effects of ingesting a pre-workout dietary supplement with and without synephrine for 8 weeks on training adaptations in resistance-trained males
authors: Y. Peter Jung, Conrad P. Earnest, Majid Koozehchian, Minye Cho, Nick Barringer, Dillon Walker, Chris...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of a pre-workout supplement with and without synephrine on resistance-trained males over 8 weeks. No significant differences were found in most training adaptations, but some improvements in cognitive function and strength were observed with the supplement.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on sow gestation: a meta-analysis
authors: Ni Wayan Helpina Widyasanti, Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, I. Putu Cahyadi Putra, Jonathan Anug...
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated vitamin E supplementation in pregnant sows. Vitamin E significantly increased serum α-tocopherol in sows and piglets, but did not affect litter size or weight.

title: Effects of Exercise Training under Hyperbaric Oxygen on Oxidative Stress Markers and Endurance Performance in Young Soccer Players: A Pilot Study
authors: Carlos Burgos, Carlos Henríquez-Olguín, David Cristóbal Andrade, Rodrigo Ramírez-Campillo, Oscar F. ...
abstract: This pilot study investigated the effects of hyperbaric oxygen training on young soccer players. The training improved endurance performance without increasing oxidative stress markers.

title: Antioxidants to Supplement or Not to Supplement That Is the Question
authors: Stanley Omaye, Nabil Elsayed

title: A blinded, placebo‐controlled study on the clinical effects of vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis
authors: Casey L. Gordon, Samantha J. Reeves, Richard K. Burchell, Craig Thomson, Arnon Gal, Nicolas Lopez‐Vi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in dogs with osteoarthritis. Vitamin E did not improve pain, lameness, quality of life, or reduce pain medication needs.

title: The effect of fish oil supplementation on resistance training-induced adaptations
authors: Jeffery L. Heileson, Steven B. Machek, Dillon R. Harris, Sara Tomek, Leticia C. de Souza, Adam J. Ki...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of fish oil supplementation on resistance training adaptations in young adults. Fish oil supplementation, compared to placebo, significantly increased bench press strength but did not significantly alter body composition or squat strength.

title: Effect of vitamin E supplementation on chicken sperm quality: A meta-analysis
authors: Sari Yanti Hayanti, Cecep Hidayat, Anuraga Jayanegara, Mohammad Miftakhus Sholikin, Supardi Rusdiana...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of dietary vitamin E on rooster sperm quality. Vitamin E supplementation significantly improved sperm concentration, motility, viability, and fertility, while reducing sperm death.

title: Effects of medium-term green tea extract supplementation combined with CrossFit workout on blood antioxidant status and serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor in young men: a pilot study
authors: Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Przemysław Domaszewski, Ilona Pokora, Aleksandra Żebrowska, Agnieszka Gdańska, T...
abstract: This pilot study examined the effects of green tea extract (GTE) and CrossFit on young men's antioxidant status and BDNF. GTE supplementation, combined with CrossFit, showed a greater increase in antioxidant capacity compared to placebo, with some improvements in antioxidant enzymes.

title: Effects of Peanut Protein Supplementation on Resistance Training Adaptations in Younger Adults
authors: Casey L. Sexton, Morgan A. Smith, Kristen S. Smith, Shelby C. Osburn, Joshua S. Godwin, Bradley A. R...
abstract: Peanut protein supplementation was studied alongside resistance training in young adults. The supplement did not affect muscle protein synthesis or strength gains in males and females.

title: Vitamin E and Bone Structural Changes: An Evidence-Based Review
authors: Isa Naina Mohamed, Boekhtiar Borhanuddin, Ahmad Nazrun Shuid, Nur Farhana Mohd Fozi
abstract: This review examined vitamin E's effects on bone structure, analyzing 11 studies. Some animal studies showed positive bone changes with vitamin E, particularly tocotrienols, suggesting potential for osteoporosis research.

title: Cornu cervi pantotrichum  supplementation improves physiological adaptions during intensive endurance training
authors: Wen-Ching HUANG, Chi-Chang HUANG, Hsiao-Li CHUANG, Chien-Chao CHIU, Wen-Chyuan CHEN, Mei-Chich HSU
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Cornu cervi pantotrichum (CCP) supplementation on mice undergoing intensive endurance training. CCP supplementation improved physiological adaptations related to fatigue and energy consumption, and maintained fat composition compared to training alone.

title: Evidence for beneficial effects of vitamin E
authors: Etsuo Niki
abstract: This review discusses vitamin E's role as an antioxidant in diseases linked to oxidative stress. Vitamin E benefits individuals with oxidative stress if administered correctly in terms of timing and duration.

title: α-Tocopherol Pharmacokinetics in Adults with Cystic Fibrosis: Benefits of Supplemental Vitamin C Administration
authors: Maret G. Traber, Scott W. Leonard, Vihas T. Vasu, Brian M. Morrissey, Huangshu (John) Lei, Jeffrey A...
abstract: This study investigated α-tocopherol pharmacokinetics in adults with cystic fibrosis, with and without vitamin C supplementation. Vitamin C administration slowed the plasma disappearance rate of α-tocopherol, suggesting it augments its concentration.

title: Temperate performance and metabolic adaptations following endurance training performed under environmental heat stress
authors: Ed Maunder, Daniel J. Plews, Gareth A. Wallis, Matthew J. Brick, Warren B. Leigh, Wee‐Leong Chang, C...
abstract: Endurance training in 33°C versus 18°C was studied in trained males. Training in heat improved time-trial performance and mitochondrial citrate synthase activity more than training in temperate conditions.

title: Beet supplementation mitigates post-exercise inflammation
authors: David C. Nieman, Camila A. Sakaguchi, James C. Williams, Fayaj A. Mulani, Patil Shivprasad Suresh, A...
abstract: A mixed beet-based supplement was tested against a placebo in cyclists after intensive exercise. The supplement increased nitrate/nitrite levels and reduced inflammation-related proteins and oxylipins post-exercise.

title: Sex differences in the effect of fish-oil supplementation on the adaptive response to resistance exercise training in older people: a randomized controlled trial 1 2
authors: Mariasole Da Boit, Rachael Sibson, Selvaraj Sivasubramaniam, Judith R Meakin, Carolyn A Greig, Richa...
source: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated fish oil supplementation's effect on resistance training adaptations in older adults, comparing men and women. Fish oil enhanced muscle strength and quality in women, but not in men, though it lowered triglycerides in both sexes.

title: Effect of vitamins C or E supplementation to Tris diluent on the semen quality of Awassi rams preserved at 5 ˚C
authors: Osama Ibrahim Azawi, Elias Khudhur Hussein
abstract: This study investigated the effect of adding vitamins C or E to a semen diluent for Awassi rams stored at 5°C. Adding vitamins C or E improved sperm motility, viability, and reduced abnormalities during storage.

title: Vitamin C: should we supplement?
authors: Angélique M.E. Spoelstra-de Man, Paul W.G. Elbers, Heleen M. Oudemans-Van Straaten
abstract: This paper reviews vitamin C's role in critically ill patients, where deficiency is common. Pharmacological doses may reduce organ dysfunction and mortality, but more research is needed.

title: Arginine and antioxidant supplement on performance in elderly male cyclists: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Steve Chen, Woosong Kim, Susanne M Henning, Catherine L Carpenter, Zhaoping Li
abstract: An L-arginine and antioxidant supplement was tested on elderly male cyclists. The supplement increased anaerobic threshold but did not affect VO2 max.

title: Prevention of Mammary Tumorigenesis in Acatalasemic Mice by Vitamin E Supplementation
authors: Kunihiko Ishii, Li‐Xue Zhen, Da‐hong Wang, Yuka Funamori, Katsuo Ogawa, Kazuhisa Taketa
source: Japanese Journal of Cancer Research : Gann
abstract: Acatalasemic mice were studied to assess vitamin E's effect on mammary tumors. Vitamin E supplementation significantly reduced mammary tumor incidence in these mice.

title: A functional evaluation of anti-fatigue and exercise performance improvement following vitamin B complex supplementation in healthy humans, a randomized double-blind trial
authors: Mon-Chien Lee, Yi-Ju Hsu, Sih-Yu Shen, Chin-Shan Ho, Chi-Chang Huang
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin B complex supplementation on exercise performance and fatigue. Supplementation significantly improved endurance and reduced fatigue markers without adverse effects.

title: Effects of arachidonic acid supplementation on training adaptations in resistance-trained males
authors: Michael D Roberts, Mike Iosia, Chad M Kerksick, Lem W Taylor, Bill Campbell, Colin D Wilborn, Travis...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated arachidonic acid (AA) supplementation's effects on resistance-trained males. AA supplementation enhanced anaerobic capacity and reduced inflammation, but did not significantly improve strength, muscle mass, or hypertrophy markers.

title: Effects of multi-ingredient supplementation on resistance training in young males
authors: Mark ET Willems, Chris W Sallis, Jonathan A Haskell
abstract: A multi-ingredient supplement was tested alongside resistance training in young males. The supplement enhanced some strength and endurance measures, but not others.

title: Vitamin E (α-tocopherol) supplementation in diabetic rats: effects on the proximal colon
authors: Luciana P Roldi, Renata VF Pereira, Eleandro A Tronchini, Gabriela V Rizo, Célia R Scoaris, Jacqueli...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation on the proximal colons of diabetic rats. Vitamin E (2%) reduced blood sugar and protected myenteric neurons, but did not alter intestinal wall structure.

title: Effects of Endurance Training on Antioxidant and Hormonal Status in Peripheral Blood of Young Healthy Men
authors: Stanimir Stojiljković, Ljubica Gavrilović, Snežana Pejić, Snežana B. Pajović, Marija Macura, Dragan ...
abstract: An 8-week endurance running program was studied in young men. The training improved antioxidant capacity and hormonal balance, indicating adaptation without persistent oxidative stress.

title: EFFECTS OF L-ASCORBIC ACID AND ALPHA-TOCOPHEROL ON BIOCHEMICAL PARAMETERS OF SWIMMING-INDUCED OXIDATIVE STRESS IN SERUM OF GUINEA PIGS
authors: Marija Bursać-Mitrović, Dragan R. Milovanović, Radoslav Mitić, Danijela Jovanović, Miroslav Sovrlić,...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of L-ascorbic acid and alpha-tocopherol on biochemical markers of oxidative stress in guinea pigs after swimming. The vitamins demonstrated protective antioxidant activity, with combined treatments showing a synergistic effect.

title: Enhanced Human Neutrophil Vitamin C Status, Chemotaxis and Oxidant Generation Following Dietary Supplementation with Vitamin C-Rich  SunGold  Kiwifruit
authors: Stephanie M. Bozonet, Anitra C. Carr, Juliet M. Pullar, Margreet C. M. Vissers
abstract: Dietary supplementation with vitamin C-rich kiwifruit was studied in men with suboptimal vitamin C status. Supplementation improved neutrophil chemotaxis and oxidant generation, suggesting enhanced immunity.

title: Does vitamin D supplementation improve bone health, body composition and physical performance beyond endurance exercise in patients with type 2 diabetes: A secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial
authors: Xiaomin Sun, Wenjuan Xiao, Zhongying Li, Sirui Zhou, Mengyue Dong, Cong Huang, Yan Ma, Bo Gou
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamin D and endurance exercise on type 2 diabetes patients. Vitamin D supplementation alone did not improve outcomes beyond exercise, but it may help prevent exercise-induced bone loss.

title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on upper and lower limb muscle strength and muscle power in athletes: A meta-analysis
authors: Lin Zhang, Minghui Quan, Zhen-Bo Cao
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of vitamin D supplementation on athlete muscle strength and power. Vitamin D supplementation positively impacted lower limb muscle strength, but not upper limb strength or muscle power.

title: Dietary and supplemental intake of vitamins C and E is associated with altered DNA methylation in an epigenome-wide association study meta-analysis
authors: Amena Keshawarz, Roby Joehanes, Jiantao Ma, Gha Young Lee, Ricardo Costeira, Pei-Chien Tsai, Olatz M...
abstract: This study meta-analyzed EWAS results to assess vitamin C and E intake's association with DNA methylation. Vitamin C intake was linked to numerous CpG sites, potentially influencing systems development and immune response.

title: Influence of Vitamin E Supplementation on Glycaemic Control: A Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials
authors: Renfan Xu, Shasha Zhang, Anyu Tao, Guangzhi Chen, Muxun Zhang
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E supplementation's effect on glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes. Vitamin E supplementation did not significantly improve HbA1c, fasting glucose, or fasting insulin, except in patients with low baseline vitamin E.

title: Effects of Vitamin D3 Supplementation and Resistance Training on 25-Hydroxyvitamin D Status and Functional Performance of Older Adults: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Rudolf Aschauer, Sandra Unterberger, Patrick A. Zöhrer, Agnes Draxler, Bernhard Franzke, Eva-Maria S...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation and resistance training on older adults. Vitamin D supplementation improved vitamin D status but did not enhance muscle performance or functional mobility beyond resistance training alone.

title: Vitamin E Dietary Supplementation Improves Neurological Symptoms and Decreases c-Abl/p73 Activation in Niemann-Pick C Mice
authors: Tamara Marín, Pablo Contreras, Juan Francisco Castro, David Chamorro, Elisa Balboa, Mònica Bosch-Mor...
abstract: Dietary vitamin E supplementation was studied in Niemann-Pick C mice to assess its impact on neurological symptoms and disease progression. The supplementation delayed neurodegeneration, improved motor function, and reduced markers of oxidative stress and apoptosis.

title: Oral vitamin C restores endothelial function during acute inflammation in young and older adults
authors: Elizabeth C. Lefferts, Brooks A. Hibner, Wesley K. Lefferts, Natalia S. Lima, Tracy Baynard, Jacob M...
abstract: Oral vitamin C was given to young and older adults during acute inflammation to assess its effect on vascular function. Vitamin C restored endothelial function, but not aortic stiffness, during inflammation.

title: Effects of antioxidant-rich  foods  on altitude-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in elite endurance athletes: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Anu Elisa Koivisto, Thomas Olsen, Ingvild Paur, Gøran Paulsen, Nasser Ezzatkhah Bastani, Ina Garthe,...
abstract: Elite endurance athletes consumed antioxidant-rich foods during altitude training. This increased antioxidant capacity and reduced some inflammatory markers, but did not affect oxidative stress.

title: Adaptations to strength training differ between endurance-trained and untrained women
authors: Olav Vikmoen, Truls Raastad, Stian Ellefsen, Bent R. Rønnestad
abstract: Endurance-trained and untrained women underwent 11 weeks of strength training. Concurrent training did not impair strength or hypertrophy gains, but attenuated increases in explosive power.

title: Does vitamin-D intake during resistance training improve the skeletal muscle hypertrophic and strength response in young and elderly men? – a randomized controlled trial
authors: Jakob Agergaard, Jeanette Trøstrup, Jacob Uth, Jonas Vestergard Iversen, Anders Boesen, Jesper L. An...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin-D's impact on muscle growth and strength during resistance training in young and elderly men. Vitamin-D supplementation did not enhance muscle hypertrophy or strength gains, though some molecular changes were observed in young men.

title: The effect of vitamin E supplementation on selected inflammatory biomarkers in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
authors: Omid Asbaghi, Mehdi Sadeghian, Behzad Nazarian, Mehrnoosh Sarreshtedari, Hassan Mozaffari-Khosravi, ...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin E's effects on inflammatory biomarkers in adults. Vitamin E, especially alpha-tocopherol, significantly reduced C-reactive protein and tumor necrosis factor-alpha levels.

title: The effects of isoflavone supplementation plus combined exercise on salivary markers of oxidative stress in postmenopausal women
authors: Ana Luiza Amaral, Anne M. Mendonça, Jéssica S. Giolo, Juliene G. Costa, Igor M. Mariano, Tállita C. ...
abstract: This study investigated isoflavone supplementation combined with exercise in postmenopausal women. Isoflavones, with exercise, reduced lipid peroxidation and salivary nitrite, suggesting an antioxidant effect.

title: A Dose-Dependent Effect of Carnipure ®  Tartrate Supplementation on Endurance Capacity, Recovery, and Body Composition in an Exercise Rat Model
authors: Kazim Sahin, Cemal Orhan, Osman Kucuk, Nurhan Sahin, Mehmet Tuzcu, Besir Er, Shane Durkee, Aouatef B...
abstract: Carnipure® Tartrate supplementation was studied in exercising rats to assess its effects on endurance, recovery, and body composition. The study found that CT supplementation dose-dependently improved endurance, recovery, and antioxidant capacity, while reducing body weight and fat.

title: Cardioprotection conferred by exercise training is blunted by blockade of the opioid system
authors: Tatiana F G Galvão, Katt C Matos, Patrícia C Brum, Carlos E Negrão, Protásio Lemos da Luz, Antônio C...
abstract: Exercise training and other interventions were studied for their cardioprotective effects. Opioid receptor blockade blunted the cardioprotective benefits of exercise training, suggesting a role for opioids in this protection.

title: Effect of thyme extract supplementation on lipid peroxidation, antioxidant capacity, PGC-1α content and endurance exercise performance in rats
authors: Mostafa Khani, Pezhman Motamedi, Mohammad Reza Dehkhoda, Saeed Dabagh Nikukheslat, Pouran Karimi
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of thyme extract supplementation on endurance exercise in rats. Thyme extract supplementation prolonged exercise tolerance but did not improve antioxidant capacity or mitochondrial biogenesis markers.

title: Efficacy of Vitamin C Supplements in Prevention of Cancer: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Bobae Lee, Seung-Won Oh, Seung-Kwon Myung
abstract: A meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials examined vitamin C supplements for cancer prevention. The analysis found no significant association between vitamin C supplementation and reduced cancer risk.

title: Inter-Individual Variability in the Adaptive Responses to Endurance and Sprint Interval Training: A Randomized Crossover Study
authors: Jacob T. Bonafiglia, Mario P. Rotundo, Jonathan P. Whittall, Trisha D. Scribbans, Ryan B. Graham, Br...
abstract: This study investigated individual responses to endurance and sprint interval training in adults. Both training types elicited varied adaptations, with no consistent response patterns between them, though all participants responded to at least one intervention.

title: Mangosteen Concentrate Drink Supplementation Promotes Antioxidant Status and Lactate Clearance in Rats after Exercise
authors: Ching-Chien Chang, Chia-Wen Chen, Eddy Owaga, Wan-Ting Lee, Ting-Ni Liu, Rong-Hong Hsieh
abstract: Mangosteen concentrate drink supplementation was studied in rats after running exercise. The drink increased antioxidant enzymes, reduced oxidative stress, and improved lactate clearance, benefiting muscle fatigue reduction.

title: Alpha-Tocopherol Metabolites (The Vitamin E Metabolome) and Their Interindividual Variability during Supplementation
authors: Desirée Bartolini, Rita Marinelli, Danilo Giusepponi, Roberta Galarini, Carolina Barola, Anna Maria ...
abstract: This study analyzed vitamin E metabolites in healthy volunteers after supplementation. Metabolite levels showed significant interindividual variability, with some metabolites being poor indicators of intake, while others correlated with vitamin E levels and gene expression.

title: Exercise without Weight Loss Prevents Seasonal Decline in Vitamin D Metabolites: The VitaDEx Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Oliver J. Perkin, Sophie E. Davies, Martin Hewison, Kerry S. Jones, Javier T. Gonzalez, James A. Bet...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial studied the effect of exercise on vitamin D metabolites in overweight adults during winter. Regular exercise maintained active vitamin D levels and may prevent declines in other vitamin D metabolites, independent of weight loss.

title: Efficacy of Vitamin and Antioxidant Supplements in Prevention of Esophageal Cancer: Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Seung-Kwon Myung, Hyo Jin Yang
abstract: This meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials on vitamin and antioxidant supplements for esophageal cancer prevention. The findings indicate no evidence that these supplements prevent esophageal cancer.

title: Carbon tetrachloride-induced liver disease in rats: the potential effect of supplement oils with vitamins E and C on the nutritional status
authors: Rasha S. A. Ismail, Ashraf A. A. El-Megeid, Aly R. Abdel-Moemin
abstract: This study investigated the effects of different oils and vitamin supplementation on carbon tetrachloride-induced liver damage in rats. Supplementing oils with vitamins E and C, particularly flaxseed oil, significantly improved liver function and histology.

title: Antioxidant trials—the need to test for stress
authors: Robert John Aitken

title: Effect of vitamin C injections on exercise muscular performance and biochemical parameters in  Trichinella spiralis -infected mice
authors: Hadeer Abd El-hak Rashed, Bander Albogami, Abdulsalam A. M. Alkhaldi, Najlaa Y. Abuzinadah, Samah S....
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C injections' effects on exercise performance and biochemical markers in mice infected with *Trichinella spiralis*. Vitamin C improved muscular performance, reduced histological damage, and ameliorated biochemical markers of oxidative stress and muscle damage.

title: Effects of Plyometric Training and Beta-Alanine Supplementation on Maximal-Intensity Exercise and Endurance in Female Soccer Players
authors: Fabián Rosas, Rodrigo Ramírez-Campillo, Cristian Martínez, Alexis Caniuqueo, Rodrigo Cañas-Jamet, Em...
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of plyometric training and beta-alanine supplementation on female soccer players. Beta-alanine supplementation alongside plyometric training enhanced endurance, repeated sprinting, and repeated jumping performance more than plyometric training alone.

title: Regular sling core stabilization training improves bone density based on calcium and vitamin D supplementation
authors: Jing Liu, Daoming Xu, Lanying Liu, Chihuan Huang, Zhijie Guo, Di Zhang, Liyu Wei
abstract: This paper reports on a case study of a 70-year-old woman with osteoporosis. Regular sling core stabilization training, combined with calcium and vitamin D supplementation, improved her bone density and relieved back pain.

title: Effect of Vitamin C and Protein Supplementation on Plasma Nitrate and Nitrite Response following Consumption of Beetroot Juice
authors: Gary D. Miller, Beverly A. Nesbit, Daniel B. Kim-Shapiro, Swati Basu, Michael J. Berry
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin C or protein supplementation on plasma nitrate and nitrite levels after beetroot juice consumption. No significant differences were found in plasma nitrate and nitrite levels when beetroot juice was co-ingested with vitamin C or whey protein compared to beetroot juice alone.

title: Building strength, endurance, and mobility using an astaxanthin formulation with functional training in elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Amir S. Ali, Matthew D. Campbell, Kevin Kilroy, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan...
source: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
abstract: An astaxanthin formulation was tested with functional training in elderly subjects. The formulation improved muscle strength and size, in addition to exercise-induced gains in endurance and mobility.

title: Effects of Zinc Magnesium Aspartate (ZMA) Supplementation on Training Adaptations and Markers of Anabolism and Catabolism
authors: Colin D Wilborn, Chad M Kerksick, Bill I Campbell, Lem W Taylor, Brandon M Marcello, Christopher J R...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated ZMA supplementation's effects on training adaptations and hormone profiles in resistance-trained males. ZMA did not significantly improve training adaptations, body composition, or hormone levels compared to placebo.

title: Iron Supplementation during Three Consecutive Days of Endurance Training Augmented Hepcidin Levels
authors: Aya Ishibashi, Naho Maeda, Akiko Kamei, Kazushige Goto
abstract: This study investigated the impact of three days of intense endurance training and iron supplementation on hepcidin levels in male athletes. Iron supplementation during this training period significantly augmented hepcidin levels compared to placebo.

title: Impact of protein supplementation during endurance training on changes in skeletal muscle transcriptome
authors: Pim Knuiman, Roland Hangelbroek, Mark Boekschoten, Maria Hopman, Marco Mensink
abstract: This study analyzed skeletal muscle transcriptome changes after endurance training with or without protein supplementation. Protein supplementation increased the number of differentially expressed genes, particularly those related to the extracellular matrix.

title: Powdered tart cherry supplementation surrounding a single bout of intense resistance exercise demonstrates potential attenuation of recovery strength decrement with no definitive oxidative or inflammatory effect
authors: K Levers, R Dalton, E Galvan, C Goodenough, A O'Connor, S Simbo, N Barringer, S Mertens-Talcott, C R...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Effect of resistance training with and without vitamin D calcium chitosan nanoparticle supplements on apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats: An experimental study
authors: Mahsa Dehghan-Manshadi, Mohammad-Ali Azarbayjani, Sirvan Atashak, Maghsoud Peeri, Saleh Rahmati-Ahma...
abstract: This study examined how resistance training and vitamin D/calcium/chitosan nanoparticles affect apoptosis markers in ovariectomized rats. The combination of resistance training and supplements appeared to reverse OVX-induced apoptosis.

title: The association of oxidative stress of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and vitamin E supplementation
authors: Mohamed Zaeim Hafez Ahmed, Reham Helmy Amin Helmy Saad, Ahmad Gadalla, Ramadan Hassan Ibrahim Thabet...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin E supplementation on neonatal hyperbilirubinemia treated with phototherapy. Vitamin E significantly reduced serum bilirubin levels and the duration of phototherapy.

title: Effects of exercise training and dietary supplement on fat free mass and bone mass density during weight loss – a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Anja Roth, Martin Sattelmayer, Chloé Schorderet, Simone Gafner, Lara Allet, Nahid Ramezani-Jolfaie, ...
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined exercise training and dietary supplements' effects on fat-free mass during weight loss. Exercise training, particularly combined with high protein intake, significantly helps preserve fat-free mass.

title: Dietary Adjustments to Altitude Training in Elite Endurance Athletes; Impact of a Randomized Clinical Trial With Antioxidant-Rich Foods
authors: Anu E. Koivisto-Mørk, Ingvild Paur, Gøran Paulsen, Ina Garthe, Truls Raastad, Nasser E. Bastani, Run...
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Elite endurance athletes increased energy, carbohydrate, iron, fluid, and antioxidant-rich food intake during altitude training. An antioxidant-rich snack intervention further boosted intake of specific nutrients but did not significantly alter blood parameters compared to a control group.

title: Combined effects of vitamin D supplementation and endurance exercise training on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with vitamin D deficiency: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Mi Xiang, Xiaomin Sun, Junxiang Wei, Zhen-Bo Cao
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating the combined effects of vitamin D and endurance exercise on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients. The research aims to determine if this combination offers synergistic benefits beyond individual interventions.

title: Effects of Endurance Training and Chlorogenic Acid on Oxidative and Nitrosative Stress Markers in Prediabetic Male Mice
authors: Sahar Ghasemi Pour, Sayyed M. Marandi
abstract: Endurance training and chlorogenic acid were studied for their effects on oxidative and nitrosative stress in prediabetic mice. Both interventions improved antioxidant capacity, with endurance training reducing glutathione and chlorogenic acid increasing total antioxidant capacity.

title: Effects of Dietary Nitrate Supplementation on Performance and Muscle Oxygenation during Resistance Exercise in Men
authors: Rachel Tan, Adam Pennell, Katherine M. Price, Sean T. Karl, Noelle G. Seekamp-Hicks, Keonabelle K. P...
abstract: This study investigated beetroot juice supplementation's effects on resistance exercise performance and muscle oxygenation. Beetroot juice improved repetitions to failure in the bench press but had no effect on other performance measures or muscle oxygenation.

title: Effects of High-Dose Vitamin D Supplementation and Physical Exercise on Vitamin D Metabolites in Professional Football Players: A Pilot Study
authors: Anna Książek, Aleksandra Zagrodna, Konrad Kowalski
abstract: This pilot study examined vitamin D metabolite changes in professional football players during and after exercise, with and without high-dose supplementation. Physical activity increased vitamin D metabolites, and supplementation further amplified these levels, suggesting rapid status improvement.

title: The effects of endurance training and thiamine supplementation on anti-fatigue during exercise
authors: Sung-Keun Choi, Seung-Hui Baek, Seung-Wook Choi
abstract: Endurance training and thiamine supplementation were studied for their anti-fatigue effects during exercise. Both interventions significantly reduced lactate and ammonia concentrations, suggesting thiamine offers similar benefits to training.

title: The Role of Vitamin E in Preventing and Treating Osteoarthritis – A Review of the Current Evidence
authors: Kok-Yong Chin, Soelaiman Ima-Nirwana
abstract: This review examines vitamin E's role in osteoarthritis, focusing on its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Evidence suggests vitamin E may slow osteoarthritis progression by reducing oxidative stress and inflammation.

title: The Relationship between Resistance Exercise Performance and Ventilatory Efficiency after Beetroot Juice Intake in Well-Trained Athletes
authors: Noemí Serra-Payá, Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Sergio Sánchez-Nuño, Lluís Albesa-Albiol, Montser...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of beetroot juice on resistance exercise performance and ventilatory efficiency in athletes. Beetroot juice improved ventilatory efficiency and resistance exercise performance, suggesting an ergogenic effect under aerobic conditions.

title: Effects of Vitamin and Antioxidant Supplements in Prevention of Bladder Cancer: a Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: So-Jung Park, Seung-Kwon Myung, Yunju Lee, Yong-Jae Lee
abstract: This meta-analysis examined vitamin and antioxidant supplements for bladder cancer prevention across fourteen RCTs. These supplements showed no preventive effect, with beta-carotene alone potentially increasing risk.

title: On the effect of vitamin C intake on human health: How to (mis)interprete the clinical evidence
authors: Jens Lykkesfeldt
abstract: This review examines clinical studies on vitamin C's health effects beyond scurvy. It concludes that ignoring vitamin C's unique pharmacokinetics leads to flawed study designs and misinterpretation of results.

title: Antioxidant Supplements and Oxidative Stress
authors: Jumana Saleh, Marvin Edeas, Harry Van Goor

title: Effects of 8 weeks of Xpand® 2X pre workout supplementation on skeletal muscle hypertrophy, lean body mass, and strength in resistance trained males
authors: Ryan P Lowery, Jordan M Joy, Joshua E Dudeck, Eduardo Oliveira de Souza, Sean A McCleary, Shawn Well...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an 8-week pre-workout supplement on resistance-trained males. The supplement significantly increased bench press strength, lean body mass, and quadriceps muscle thickness compared to a placebo.

title: Combined effect of high-dose vitamin A, vitamin E supplementation, and zinc on adult patients with diabetes: A randomized trial
authors: Eman Said, Shrook Mousa, May Fawzi, Nirmeen A. Sabry, Samar Farid
abstract: This randomized trial investigated the effects of vitamin A plus E supplementation, with and without zinc, on adult patients with type 2 diabetes. The combination of vitamins A and E with zinc significantly improved glycemic control and insulin secretion compared to a control group.

title: Shatavari supplementation during eight weeks of resistance training increases training load, enhances skeletal muscle contractility and alters the skeletal muscle proteome in older women
authors: Elsa Greed, Jack Pritchard, Lauren Struszczak, Esra Bozbaş, Georgia Ek, Jordan Acheson, Ben Winney, ...
abstract: Shatavari supplementation was studied in older women undergoing resistance training. It increased training load, improved muscle relaxation speed, and altered muscle protein expression, suggesting reduced neuromuscular fatigue.

title: Exercise Performance Upregulatory Effect of R-α-Lipoic Acid with γ-Cyclodextrin
authors: Yuki Hashimoto, Katsuhiko Yoshizawa, Yuka Kaido, Akiko Takenouchi, Keiji Terao, Hiroyuki Yasui, Yuta...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of a γ-cyclodextrin complex of R-α-lipoic acid on exercise performance and oxidative stress in mice. The complex supplementation repressed exercise-induced blood ammonia elevation and reduced kidney oxidative stress, suggesting potential benefits for athletic performance.

title: No effect of beetroot juice supplementation on exercise economy and performance in recreationally active females despite increased torque production
authors: Kate A. Wickham, Devin G. McCarthy, Jamie M. Pereira, Daniel T. Cervone, Lex B. Verdijk, Luc J. C. v...
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice supplementation's impact on exercise economy and performance in recreationally active females. Beetroot juice did not improve exercise economy or time trial performance, despite increasing low-frequency torque production.

title: The effect of methyl sulphonyl methane supplementation on biomarkers of oxidative stress in sport horses following jumping exercise
authors: Gonzalo Marañón, Bárbara Muñoz-Escassi, William Manley, Cruz García, Patricia Cayado, Mercedes Sánch...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of methyl sulfonyl methane (MSM) and vitamin C supplementation on oxidative stress markers in sport horses after jumping exercise. MSM supplementation, especially when combined with vitamin C, significantly reduced exercise-induced increases in oxidative stress and inflammation.

title: Effects of Urolithin A supplementation on performance and antioxidant status in academy soccer players during preseason: a pilot randomised controlled trial
authors: Andrea Monsalve Acevedo, Colin Sanctuary, Robert John Aitken, Alex Wilkins, Natasha Harrison, Mitche...
abstract: This pilot study investigated Urolithin A supplementation in academy soccer players during preseason training. Urolithin A supplementation significantly improved aerobic endurance compared to placebo.

title: Vitamins C and E alleviate the deleterious effects of electronic cigarettes on tongue muscles and nerves in rat model
authors: Yasmine M. Tolba, Raghda A. Abou ayana, Dina A. Nagui
abstract: This study investigated electronic cigarette effects on rat tongue muscles and nerves, and the protective roles of vitamins C and E. Vitamins E and C, but not C alone, significantly mitigated electronic cigarette-induced oxidative damage and ultrastructural harm.

title: Cranberry supplementation improves physiological markers of performance in trained runners
authors: Francis Parenteau, Veronica Furno Puglia, Mary Roberts, Alain Steve Comtois, Andreas Bergdahl
abstract: This study investigated cranberry extract's effects on trained runners' performance and physiological markers. Chronic supplementation improved running performance and muscle reoxygenation, and buffered lactate response during shorter races.

title: Beetroot supplementation in women enjoying exercise together (BEE SWEET): Rationale, design and methods
authors: Marissa N. Baranauskas, Cody A. Altherr, Allison H. Gruber, Andrew R. Coggan, John S. Raglin, Samir ...
abstract: This study investigates if beetroot supplementation enhances exercise benefits in postmenopausal women. It aims to determine if beetroot juice improves mobility and cardiovascular health outcomes compared to exercise alone or exercise with a placebo.

title: Effects of Vitamin E on Cognitive Performance during Ageing and in Alzheimer’s Disease
authors: Giorgio La Fata, Peter Weber, M. Hasan Mohajeri
