abstract: This review examines vitamin E's role in cognitive performance during aging and Alzheimer's disease. Inconsistent study outcomes mean vitamin E's benefit for neurodegenerative disorders remains debated.

title: High-dose testosterone supplementation disturbs liver pro-oxidant/antioxidant balance and function in adolescent male Wistar rats undergoing moderate-intensity endurance training
authors: Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Barbara Kłapcińska, Anna Nowara, Sławomir Jagsz, Izabela Szołtysek-Bołdys, Małgo...
abstract: High-dose testosterone supplementation was studied in adolescent rats undergoing endurance training. It disrupted the liver's antioxidant balance and function, increasing oxidative stress markers and enzyme activities.

title: Antioxidant supplementation in hypertension
authors: Mohammad Reza Ardalan, Mahmoud Rafieian-Kopaei

title: Effects of β-Alanine Supplementation on Subjects Performing High-Intensity Functional Training
authors: Eduardo Cimadevilla-Fernández-Pola, Cristina Martínez-Roldán, Jose Luis Maté-Muñoz, Jesús Guodemar-P...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of four weeks of β-alanine supplementation on individuals performing High-Intensity Functional Training. β-alanine supplementation improved vertical jump and jumping power without significantly altering fatigue or perceived exertion.

title: Vitamin E and Alzheimer’s Disease—Is It Time for Personalized Medicine?
authors: Breana Cervantes, Lynn M. Ulatowski
abstract: This paper reviews the debate on vitamin E's efficacy for Alzheimer's disease, considering different forms, combination treatments, and safety. It proposes that genetic variations influencing vitamin E metabolism may necessitate a personalized medicine approach for future clinical trials.

title: Vitamin C Is Essential for the Maintenance of Skeletal Muscle Functions
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Yuka Takino, Jaewon Lee, Shuichi Machida, Akihito Ishigami
abstract: Long-term vitamin C deficiency was studied in male mice lacking VC synthesis, showing muscle atrophy and reduced physical ability. Vitamin C is essential for maintaining skeletal muscle function in both sexes.

title: Vitamin E Supplementation with  Rauwolfia Vomitoria  Root Bark Extract Improves Hematological Indices
authors: Akpanabiatu Monday Isaiah, Otitoju Olawale, Edet Emmanuel Effiong, Ndem Jessie Idongesit, Uwah Antho...
source: North American Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E supplementation with *Rauwolfia vomitoria* root bark extract on rat hematology. The combination improved immunity and enhanced hematological indices, suggesting a therapeutic interaction.

title: Reply: antioxidant trials—the need to test for stress
authors: Mohan S Kamath, Mariano Mascarenhas, Treasa Joseph, Muthukumar Karthikeyan, Aleyamma T Kunjummen

title: Effects of 𝛽-Hydroxy-𝛽-methylbutyrate-free Acid Supplementation on Strength, Power and Hormonal Adaptations Following Resistance Training
authors: Abbas Asadi, Hamid Arazi, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This study investigated the effects of HMB-FA supplementation during resistance training on strength, power, and hormonal responses in men. HMB-FA supplementation enhanced power and strength gains and positively influenced growth hormone and IGF-1 levels, while reducing ACTH and cortisol.

title: Vitamin E and Alzheimer’s disease: what do we know so far?
authors: Declan Browne, Bernadette McGuinness, Jayne V Woodside, Gareth J McKay
abstract: This paper reviews the potential of vitamin E for Alzheimer's disease, examining its biological functions and observed deficiencies. Despite a strong theoretical basis, clinical trial evidence for vitamin E supplementation remains inconclusive due to various factors.

title: The Effect of Beta-Alanine versus Alkaline Agent Supplementation Combined with Branched-Chain Amino Acids and Creatine Malate in Highly-Trained Sprinters and Endurance Athletes: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover Study
authors: Krzysztof Durkalec-Michalski, Krzysztof Kusy, Monika Ciekot-Sołtysiak, Jacek Zieliński
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beta-alanine versus alkaline agents, combined with BCAAs and creatine malate, on elite sprinters and endurance athletes. Beta-alanine supplementation led to increased fat-free mass in sprinters and reduced post-exercise ammonia in both groups, but did not improve aerobic capacity.

title: The effect on endothelial function of vitamin C during methionine induced hyperhomocysteinaemia
authors: Colm G Hanratty, Lawrence T McGrath, Daniel F McAuley, Ian S Young, Dennis G Johnston
abstract: Methionine increased homocysteine and impaired endothelial function in healthy adults. Vitamin C did not prevent this impairment, suggesting the mechanism is not free radical-mediated.

title: Vitamin C—Sources, Physiological Role, Kinetics, Deficiency, Use, Toxicity, and Determination
authors: Martin Doseděl, Eduard Jirkovský, Kateřina Macáková, Lenka Kujovská Krčmová, Lenka Javorská, Jana Po...
abstract: This review discusses vitamin C's broad physiological roles beyond its antioxidant function, including its impact on iron absorption and epigenetic processes. While essential for preventing scurvy, high doses can be pro-oxidant and potentially harmful, with limited proven benefits for other diseases.

title: Effect of vitamin e supplementation with exercise on cognitive functions and total antioxidant capacity in older people
authors: E. Çetin; E.C. Top; G. Şahin; Y. Gül. Özkaya; H. Aydin; F. Toraman
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: We investigated the effects of six months vitamin E administration on cognition evaluated by event-related potentials in exercising older subjects. Randomised controlled trial. Retirement home in Anta

title: Does  Colostrum Bovinum  Supplementation Affect Swimming Performance in Endurance-Trained Males? A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Study
authors: Krzysztof Durkalec-Michalski, Natalia Główka, Tomasz Podgórski, Mikołaj Szymocha, Błażej Przybylik, ...
abstract: Colostrum Bovinum supplementation was studied for its effects on swimming performance and exercise adaptations in endurance-trained males. Colostrum Bovinum and placebo were found to be comparably effective in evoking exercise adaptations, with no significant impact on swimming performance.

title: Effects of electrotactic exercise and antioxidant EUK-134 on oxidative stress relief in  Caenorhabditis elegans
authors: Thi Thanh Huong Pham, Wan-Ying Huang, Chang-Shi Chen, Wen-Tai Chiu, Han-Sheng Chuang
abstract: Electrotactic exercise and antioxidant EUK-134 were studied for their effects on oxidative stress in *C. elegans*. The combination significantly improved worm survivorship, reproduction, and motility, suggesting long-term antioxidative stress benefits.

title: Beetroot Juice Supplementation Improves High-Intensity Intermittent Type Exercise Performance in Trained Soccer Players
authors: Jean Nyakayiru, Kristin L. Jonvik, Jorn Trommelen, Philippe J. M. Pinckaers, Joan M. Senden, Luc J. ...
abstract: Six days of beetroot juice supplementation were studied in trained soccer players. This supplementation improved high-intensity intermittent exercise performance and reduced heart rate.

title: Effects of  Cistanche deserticola  Y.C. Ma Supplementation on Muscle Strength and Recovery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Biaoxu Tao, Weihao Lian, Rongrong Min, Xiaoyu Zhang, Liqi Chen, Sun Hao, Ze Li, Chengzhe Ma, Haojie ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of *Cistanche deserticola* supplementation on muscle strength and recovery in trained and untrained men. Supplementation significantly improved muscle strength, endurance, and recovery markers in both groups.

title: Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation Enhances Intermittent Running Performance but Does Not Reduce Oxygen Cost of Exercise among Recreational Adults
authors: Ozcan Esen, Raúl Domínguez, Raci Karayigit
abstract: Acute beetroot juice supplementation was studied for its effects on intermittent running performance and oxygen cost. It improved performance but did not reduce oxygen consumption in recreational adults.

title: Supplementation with  Lactiplantibacillus brevis  GKEX Combined with Resistance Exercise Training Improves Muscle Mass, Strength Performance, and Body Fat Condition in Healthy Humans
authors: Mon-Chien Lee, Yi-Ju Hsu, Chin-Shan Ho, You-Shan Tsai, Chin-Chu Chen, Chi-Chang Huang
abstract: This study investigated the effects of *Lactiplantibacillus brevis* GKEX supplementation combined with resistance training. The combination significantly improved muscle mass, strength, and reduced body fat compared to placebo.

title: Acute effects of beetroot juice vs. creatine supplementation on maximal strength, autonomic regulation, and muscle oxygenation during incremental resistance exercise
authors: Atef Salem, Achraf Ammar, Mohamed Kerkeni, Mohamed Ali Boujelbane, Ayse Merve Uyar, Leonard Moritz K...
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice and creatine supplementation's acute effects on strength, autonomic regulation, and muscle oxygenation during resistance exercise. Beetroot juice improved muscle oxygenation and autonomic regulation compared to placebo, while both supplements enhanced peak velocity.

title: Effect of an herbal/botanical supplement on strength, balance, and muscle function following 12-weeks of resistance training: a placebo controlled study
authors: Jonathan Furlong, Corey A Rynders, Mark Sutherlin, James Patrie, Frank I Katch, Jay Hertel, Arthur W...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: A 12-week resistance training program was studied with and without an herbal supplement. The supplement did not enhance strength, balance, or muscle function adaptations beyond those from training alone.

title: The effect of long term astaxanthin supplementation on the antioxidant status of racing Arabian horses – preliminary study
authors: Beata Giercuszkiewicz-Hecold, Marek Kulka, Michał Czopowicz, Jacek Wilczak, Ewa Szarska, Katarzyna S...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of long-term astaxanthin supplementation on racing Arabian horses. Astaxanthin supplementation improved antioxidant status and partially counterbalanced training-induced oxidative stress.

title: The Effects of Isoflavone Supplementation Plus Combined Exercise on Lipid Levels, and Inflammatory and Oxidative Stress Markers in Postmenopausal Women
authors: Jéssica S. Giolo, Juliene G. Costa, Jair P. da Cunha-Junior, Ana Cláudia A. M. Pajuaba, Ernesto A. T...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of isoflavone supplementation combined with exercise on postmenopausal women's lipid levels, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Isoflavone supplementation did not enhance exercise benefits; however, exercise alone may improve cholesterol and IL-8 levels.

title: Protein Supplementation Has Minimal Effects on Muscle Adaptations during Resistance Exercise Training in Young Men: A Double-Blind Randomized Clinical Trial 1 2 3
authors: Paul T Reidy, Michael S Borack, Melissa M Markofski, Jared M Dickinson, Rachel R Deer, Syed H Husain...
abstract: A randomized trial examined protein blend supplementation during resistance training in young men. Protein supplementation showed minimal effects on muscle strength and size, with only a slight trend for increased lean body mass.

title: Vitamin D and Exercise Performance in Professional Soccer Players
authors: Nikolaos E. Koundourakis, Nikolaos E. Androulakis, Niki Malliaraki, Andrew N. Margioris
abstract: This study examined the association between vitamin D levels and performance in professional soccer players, and how off-season affects vitamin D. Higher vitamin D correlated with better strength, speed, and aerobic capacity, while off-season increased vitamin D but decreased performance.

title: Association of vitamin C, vitamin D, vitamin E and risk of bladder cancer: a dose-response meta-analysis
authors: Fuqiang Chen, Qingshu Li, Yang Yu, Wenrong Yang, Fei Shi, Yan Qu
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the link between vitamins C, D, and E and bladder cancer risk. Higher vitamin D and E intake, particularly alpha-tocopherol, may reduce risk, while gamma-tocopherol might increase it, with effects more pronounced in smokers.

title: Effects of Royal Jelly Administration on Endurance Training-Induced Mitochondrial Adaptations in Skeletal Muscle
authors: Yumiko Takahashi, Kamiyu Hijikata, Kohei Seike, Suguru Nakano, Mai Banjo, Yosuke Sato, Kenya Takahas...
abstract: Royal jelly was administered to mice undergoing endurance training to study its effects on muscle mitochondria. Royal jelly enhanced training-induced mitochondrial adaptations in soleus muscles by activating AMPK.

title: The effect of Vitamin E supplementation on treatment of chronic periodontitis
authors: Parichehr Behfarnia, Mina Dadmehr, Seyedeh Negin Hosseini, Seyed Amir Mirghaderi
abstract: This study investigated Vitamin E supplementation's effect on chronic periodontitis treatment. Vitamin E significantly reduced attachment loss compared to standard treatment alone.

title: Effects of Exercise Combined with Undenatured Type II Collagen on Endurance Capacity, Antioxidant Status, Muscle Lipogenic Genes and E3 Ubiquitin Ligases in Rats
authors: Cemal Orhan, Emre Sahin, Besir Er, Mehmet Tuzcu, Andrey P. Lopes, Nurhan Sahin, Vijaya Juturu, Kazim...
abstract: Exercise combined with undenatured type II collagen improved endurance capacity and antioxidant status in rats. It also reduced muscle lipogenic gene expression and markers of muscle damage.

title: Betalain-Rich Concentrate Supplementation Improves Exercise Performance in Competitive Runners
authors: Justin S. Van Hoorebeke, Casey O. Trias, Brian A. Davis, Christina F. Lozada, Gretchen A. Casazza
abstract: This study investigated the effects of betalain-rich concentrate supplementation on competitive runners. Supplementation improved 5-km time trial performance, reduced heart rate and perceived exertion, and decreased muscle damage markers.

title: Twelve‐Week  Colostrum Bovinum  Supplementation Supports Aerobic Capacity but has No Effect on Body Composition in Endurance‐Trained Males: A Randomized Placebo‐Controlled Crossover Study
authors: Krzysztof Durkalec‐Michalski, Natalia Główka, Tomasz Podgórski, Krystian Wochna, Małgorzata Woźniewi...
abstract: Twelve-week colostrum supplementation was studied in endurance-trained males. Colostrum improved aerobic capacity indicators but did not affect body composition or time to exhaustion.

title: Acute beetroot juice supplementation does not attenuate knee extensor exercise muscle fatigue in a healthy young population
authors: Seungyong Lee, Mark G. Abel, Travis Thomas, T. Brock Symons, James W. Yates
abstract: This study investigated the effect of beetroot juice on knee extensor muscle fatigue. Beetroot juice did not reduce fatigue but did increase blood pressure in healthy young adults.

title: The effects of nutritional supplementation on older sarcopenic individuals who engage in resistance training: a meta-analysis
authors: Zixian Song, Tingting Pan, Xu Tong, Ying Yang, Ze Zhang
abstract: This meta-analysis examined resistance training with nutritional supplementation for sarcopenia. Combining resistance training with supplements, particularly protein and vitamin D, improved grip strength in older adults with sarcopenia.

title: Low‐Dose Lemon Myrtle Supplementation Enhances Muscle Hypertrophy in Older Adults Undergoing Low‐Load Resistance Training: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Risa Mitsuhashi, Shuji Sawada, Azusa Nishino, Shinichi Honda, Yuji Tominaga, Shiori Makio, Hayao Oza...
abstract: Low-dose lemon myrtle supplementation was studied with low-load resistance training in older adults. The supplement enhanced muscle growth after training but did not maintain it during detraining.

title: Vitamin E function and requirements in relation to PUFA
authors: Daniel Raederstorff, Adrian Wyss, Philip C. Calder, Peter Weber, Manfred Eggersdorfer
abstract: This review evaluated vitamin E requirements in relation to dietary PUFA intake. Vitamin E requirements increase with higher PUFA consumption and unsaturation, necessitating adequate intake to match recommended PUFA levels.

title: Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation Attenuates Morning-Associated Decrements in Supramaximal Exercise Performance in Trained Sprinters
authors: Amanda M. Dumar, Anna F. Huntington, Rebecca R. Rogers, Thomas J. Kopec, Tyler D. Williams, Christop...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of beetroot juice on morning exercise performance in sprinters. Beetroot juice supplementation prevented the typical morning performance decrements observed in trained sprinters.

title: Effects of Aerobic Dance Exercise and Honey Supplementation Followed by Their Subsequent Cessation on Bone Metabolism Markers and Antioxidant Status in Young Collegiate Females
authors: Somayeh Sadat Tavafzadeh, Chee Keong Chen, Foong Kiew Ooi, Nurul Azuar Hamzah, Siti Amrah Sulaiman, ...
abstract: This study examined the effects of aerobic dance and honey supplementation, and their cessation, on bone health and antioxidant status in young women. Combined exercise and honey supplementation improved bone and antioxidant markers, with some benefits maintained after cessation.

title: Oral Arginine Supplementation in Healthy Individuals Performing Regular Resistance Training
authors: Ștefan-Sebastian Busnatu, Octavian Andronic, Maria-Alexandra Pană, Anca Pantea Stoian, Alexandru Sca...
abstract: Oral arginine supplementation was studied in healthy men performing resistance training. Arginine supplementation reduced blood pressure and improved body composition compared to a control group.

title: Effects of supplementation with α-tocopherol, ascorbic acid, selenium, or their combination in linseed oil-enriched diets on the oxidative status in broilers
authors: J Leskovec, A Levart, A Nemec Svete, L Perić, M Đukić Stojčić, D Žikić, J Salobir, V Rezar
abstract: Broilers fed linseed oil-enriched diets were supplemented with vitamin E, vitamin C, selenium, or a combination. Vitamin E was the most effective antioxidant, with no clear synergistic benefit from adding vitamin C and selenium.

title: Prolonged Heat Acclimation and Aerobic Performance in Endurance Trained Athletes
authors: C. Jacob Mikkelsen, Nicklas Junge, Jacob F. Piil, Nathan B. Morris, Laura Oberholzer, Christoph Sieb...
abstract: This study investigated prolonged heat acclimation's effects on endurance cyclists' aerobic performance in cool conditions. Prolonged heat training did not improve aerobic power or time trial performance in cool weather compared to standard training.

title: Vitamin C for Cardiac Protection during Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Sher Ali Khan, Sandipan Bhattacharjee, Muhammad Owais Abdul Ghani, Rachel Walden, Qin M. Chen
abstract: This systematic review analyzed eight randomized controlled trials on vitamin C's effect on cardiac protection during percutaneous coronary intervention. Vitamin C administration before PCI was found to reduce cardiac injury markers and inflammation.

title: Tocotrienols and Whey Protein Isolates Substantially Increase Exercise Endurance Capacity in Diet -Induced Obese Male Sprague-Dawley Rats
authors: Andrew C. Betik, Jay Aguila, Glenn K. McConell, Andrew J. McAinch, Michael L. Mathai
abstract: This study investigated the effects of tocotrienols (TCT) and whey protein isolates (WPI) on exercise endurance in obese rats. Both TCT and WPI significantly increased exercise capacity by over 50% without affecting weight, adiposity, or glucose tolerance.

title: Four months vitamin D supplementation to vitamin D insufficient individuals does not improve muscular strength: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Guri Grimnes, Julia Kubiak, Rolf Jorde
abstract: This study investigated the effect of vitamin D supplementation on muscle strength in vitamin D insufficient individuals. Four months of supplementation did not improve muscle strength compared to placebo.

title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
authors: Robert W Morton, Kevin T Murphy, Sean R McKellar, Brad J Schoenfeld, Menno Henselmans, Eric Helms, A...
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis examined protein supplementation's effect on resistance training gains. Protein supplementation significantly increased muscle mass and strength, with benefits varying by age and training experience.

title: Consumption of Nitrate-Rich Beetroot Juice with or without Vitamin C Supplementation Increases the Excretion of Urinary Nitrate, Nitrite, and  N -nitroso Compounds in Humans
authors: Julia E. Berends, Lauri M.M. van den Berg, Martina A. Guggeis, Nikki F.T. Henckens, Israt J. Hossein...
abstract: Beetroot juice consumption increased urinary nitrate, nitrite, and N-nitroso compounds. Vitamin C supplementation reduced N-nitroso compound increase after a single dose but not after chronic use.

title: Comparative Bioavailability of Vitamin C After Short-Term Consumption of Raw Fruits and Vegetables and Their Juices: A Randomized Crossover Study
authors: Mijoo Choi, Juha Baek, Jung-Mi Yun, Young-Shick Hong, Eunju Park
abstract: This study compared vitamin C bioavailability from supplements, raw produce, and juice. Juice provided the most efficient vitamin C absorption, though all forms were bioavailable.

title: Effects of low-dose ibuprofen supplementation and resistance training on bone and muscle in postmenopausal women: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Whitney R.D. Duff, Saija A. Kontulainen, Darren G. Candow, Julianne J. Gordon, Riley S. Mason, Regin...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training and ibuprofen on bone and muscle in postmenopausal women. Ibuprofen supplementation showed some benefits for bone health, particularly when combined with stretching.

title: Effects of Protein Supplementation During High-Intensity Functional Training on Physical Performance in Recreationally Trained Males and Females: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Christina Karpouzi, Ioannis Kosmidis, Anatoli Petridou, Gabriela Voulgaridou, Sousana K. Papadopoulo...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of egg white and whey protein supplementation during High-Intensity Functional Training (HIFT). Protein supplementation did not enhance physical performance improvements from HIFT.

title: Early morning run-training results in enhanced endurance performance adaptations in mice
authors: Stuart J. Hesketh, Casey L. Sexton, Christopher A. Wolff, Mark R. Viggars, Karyn A. Esser
abstract: Six weeks of endurance training in mice showed that morning training led to greater adaptation than afternoon training. This suggests morning exercise improves muscle clock alignment for better performance.

title: Muscle-Related Effect of Whey Protein and Vitamin D 3  Supplementation Provided before or after Bedtime in Males Undergoing Resistance Training
authors: Yan Chen, Yiheng Liang, Hang Guo, Kun Meng, Junqiang Qiu, Dan Benardot
abstract: This study examined the effects of whey protein and vitamin D supplementation before or after sleep on muscle mass and strength during resistance training. Both supplementation timings led to significant improvements in muscle mass and hormones compared to a placebo.

title: A High Vitamin C Micronutrient Supplement Is Unable to Attenuate Inflammation in People with Metabolic Syndrome but May Improve Metabolic Health Indices: A Randomised Controlled Trial
authors: Emma Vlasiuk, Masuma Zawari, Rebekah Whitehead, Jonathan Williman, Anitra C. Carr
abstract: A randomized controlled trial investigated if a high vitamin C supplement could reduce inflammation in people with metabolic syndrome. The supplement did not reduce inflammation but showed minor improvements in BMI, fasting glucose, and HbA1c.

title: Dose Response of Acute ATP Supplementation on Strength Training Performance
authors: Helton Pereira dos Santos Nunes de Moura, Ralf Jäger, Martin Purpura, John A. Rathmacher, John C. Fu...
abstract: This study investigated the dose response of acute oral ATP supplementation on strength training performance. A 400 mg dose of ATP significantly increased repetitions, while 100 mg reduced perceived exertion.

title: The Effect of Nordic Walking Training Combined with Vitamin D Supplementation on Postural Control and Muscle Strength in Elderly People—A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Jan Mieszkowski, Bartłomiej Niespodziński, Andrzej Kochanowicz, Anna Gmiat, Krzysztof Prusik, Katarz...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of Nordic Walking intensity and Vitamin D supplementation on elderly women. High-intensity Nordic Walking improved Vitamin D and muscle strength, while moderate-intensity Nordic Walking showed similar Vitamin D benefits with higher supplementation, also increasing leg muscle mass.

title: Effects of an Aqueous Extract of  Withania somnifera  on Strength Training Adaptations and Recovery: The STAR Trial
authors: Tim N. Ziegenfuss, Anurag W. Kedia, Jennifer E. Sandrock, Betsy J. Raub, Chad M. Kerksick, Hector L....
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an aqueous *Withania somnifera* extract on strength training. The extract significantly improved strength gains, body composition, and recovery compared to placebo.

title: Effects of ovariectomy and resistance training on oxidative stress markers in the rat liver
authors: Maria Fernanda Cury Rodrigues, Uliana Sbeguen Stotzer, Mateus Moraes Domingos, Rafael Deminice, Gilb...
abstract: This study investigated resistance training's effects on liver oxidative stress in ovariectomized rats. The training did not reduce oxidative stress and worsened the oxidative balance in these rats.

title: Strength Training Prior to Endurance Exercise: Impact on the Neuromuscular System, Endurance Performance and Cardiorespiratory Responses
authors: Matheus Conceição, Eduardo Lusa Cadore, Miriam González-Izal, Mikel Izquierdo, Giane Veiga Liedtke, ...
abstract: This study examined strength training's acute effects on neuromuscular and cardiorespiratory responses during endurance exercise. Strength training before endurance exercise impaired time-to-exhaustion, with no significant changes in oxygen uptake or heart rate.

title: Effect of whey vs. soy protein supplementation on recovery kinetics following speed endurance training in competitive male soccer players: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Savvas Kritikos, Konstantinos Papanikolaou, Dimitrios Draganidis, Athanasios Poulios, Kalliopi Georg...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Whey and soy protein supplementation were studied for their effects on recovery after soccer speed-endurance training. Neither protein source improved performance or muscle damage markers compared to placebo.

title: Effects of gamma oryzanol supplementation on anthropometric measurements & muscular strength in healthy males following chronic resistance training
authors: Saghar Eslami, Norhaizan Mohd Esa, Seyed Mohammad Marandi, Gholamali Ghasemi, Sepehr Eslami
source: The Indian Journal of Medical Research
abstract: This study investigated gamma oryzanol supplementation's effects on strength and body measurements during resistance training. Gamma oryzanol improved muscular strength but did not significantly alter anthropometric measurements.

title: Lung Function and Respiratory Muscle Adaptations of Endurance- and Strength-Trained Males
authors: Daniel A. Hackett
abstract: This study compared lung function and respiratory muscle strength in endurance-trained versus strength-trained males. Endurance trainers showed greater maximal voluntary ventilation, while strength trainers had greater respiratory muscle strength, which was linked to lower body strength.

title: Vitamin E As a Potential Interventional Treatment for Metabolic Syndrome: Evidence from Animal and Human Studies
authors: Sok Kuan Wong, Kok-Yong Chin, Farihah Hj Suhaimi, Fairus Ahmad, Soelaiman Ima-Nirwana
abstract: This review examines evidence from animal and human studies on vitamin E's effects on metabolic syndrome. Vitamin E shows promise in reducing metabolic syndrome and its associated conditions.

title: The effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on skeletal muscle and strength adaptations in older individuals
authors: Donald A. Lamb, Johnathon H. Moore, Morgan A. Smith, Christopher G. Vann, Shelby C. Osburn, Bradley ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of resistance training with or without peanut protein supplementation on muscle and strength in older adults. Peanut protein supplementation showed some benefits in muscle thickness and strength, but not overall body composition or acute muscle protein synthesis.

title: A Comparison of Natural (D-α-tocopherol) and Synthetic (DL-α-tocopherol Acetate) Vitamin E Supplementation on the Growth Performance, Meat Quality and Oxidative Status of Broilers
authors: K. Cheng, Y. Niu, X. C. Zheng, H. Zhang, Y. P. Chen, M. Zhang, X. X. Huang, L. L. Zhang, Y. M. Zhou,...
abstract: This study compared natural and synthetic vitamin E supplementation in broilers. Natural vitamin E enhanced muscle α-tocopherol retention, improved meat quality, and boosted antioxidant capacity more than synthetic vitamin E.

title: Sustained Endurance Training Leads to Metabolomic Adaptation
authors: Astrid Weiss, Katharina Alack, Stephan Klatt, Sven Zukunft, Ralph Schermuly, Torsten Frech, Frank-Ch...
abstract: This study compared the metabolomic profiles of endurance-trained and untrained individuals. Endurance training leads to distinct changes in phospholipids, acylcarnitines, bile acids, and polyunsaturated fatty acids at rest.

title: Acute beetroot juice supplementation improves exercise tolerance and cycling efficiency in adults with obesity
authors: Christian E. Behrens, Khandaker Ahmed, Karina Ricart, Braxton Linder, José Fernández, Brenda Bertran...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on exercise in adults with obesity. Beetroot juice improved exercise efficiency and tolerance compared to other conditions.

title: Biochemical and Clinical Effects of Vitamin E Supplementation in Hungarian Smith-Lemli-Opitz Syndrome Patients
authors: Katalin Koczok, László Horváth, Zeljka Korade, Zoltán András Mezei, Gabriella P. Szabó, Ned A. Porte...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E supplementation in six SLOS patients already on cholesterol treatment. Vitamin E supplementation improved some behavioral and physical symptoms in half of the patients, particularly those with a lower baseline 7-DHC + 8-DHC/cholesterol ratio.

title: The effects of supplementation with  P-Synephrine  alone and in combination with caffeine on resistance exercise performance
authors: Nicholas A. Ratamess, Jill A. Bush, Jie Kang, William J. Kraemer, Sidney J. Stohs, Vincenzo G. Nocer...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of p-synephrine alone and with caffeine on resistance exercise performance. Supplementation with p-synephrine and caffeine significantly increased repetitions and volume load, particularly in later sets.

title: Various Effects of Omega 3 and Omega 3 Plus Vitamin E Supplementations on Serum Glucose Level and Insulin Resistance in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease
authors: Somayeh SABOORI, Mahmoud DJALALI, Esmaeil YOUSEFI RAD, Ebrahim Nematipour, Ali Akbar SABOOR-YARAGHI,...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of omega 3 and vitamin E supplementation on glucose and insulin levels in coronary artery disease patients. Co-administering omega 3 and vitamin E beneficially decreased insulin and insulin resistance, while omega 3 alone increased glucose.

title: The effect of supplementation with vitamins A, B, C, D, and E on disease severity and inflammatory responses in patients with COVID-19: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Mohammad Taghi Beigmohammadi, Sama Bitarafan, Azin Hoseindokht, Alireza Abdollahi, Laya Amoozadeh, D...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin A, B, C, D, and E supplementation on COVID-19 patients in the ICU. Vitamin supplementation improved inflammatory markers and disease severity, but did not significantly affect mortality or prolonged hospitalization after adjustments.

title: The effects of d-aspartic acid supplementation in resistance-trained men over a three month training period: A randomised controlled trial
authors: Geoffrey W. Melville, Jason C. Siegler, Paul W. M. Marshall
abstract: This study investigated the effects of d-aspartic acid supplementation on resistance-trained men over three months. D-aspartic acid did not alter testosterone levels but reduced estradiol, while both groups saw similar strength and muscle growth.

title: Training and Adaptation of Beef Calves to Precision Supplementation Technology for Individual Supplementation in Grazing Systems
authors: Joshua L. Jacobs, Matt J. Hersom, John G. Andrae, Susan K. Duckett
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: Beef calves were trained to use precision feeders for individual supplementation. The study assessed adaptation rates and feeding patterns of different calf groups to this technology.

title: Combined Effects of Exercise and Broccoli Supplementation on Metabolic and Lipoprotein Biomarkers in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Maryam Delfan, Masoumeh Gharedaghi, Farzaneh Zeynali, Rawad El Hage, Anthony C. Hackney, Halil İbrah...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise and broccoli supplementation on T2DM adults. Combining both interventions yielded the most significant improvements in metabolic and lipoprotein biomarkers.

title: Beetroot Plus Vitamin C for Performance and Recovery: Protocol of a Double‐Blind, Placebo‐Controlled, Randomized Crossover Trial in Semi‐Professional Wrestlers
authors: Maedeh Nojoumi; Alireza Hosseini Kakhki; Mohammad Ali Sardar; Ali Jafari; Ali Jafarzadeh Esfehani; R...
abstract: This study protocol outlines a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial investigating beetroot and vitamin C supplementation in semi-professional wrestlers. It aims to assess the effects on anaerobic power, fatigue, and recovery markers. The research will use Wingate tests to measure performance changes.

title: A Single Dose of Beetroot Juice Does Not Change Blood Pressure Response Mediated by Acute Aerobic Exercise in Hypertensive Postmenopausal Women
authors: Ana Luiza Amaral, Igor M. Mariano, Victor Hugo V. Carrijo, Tállita Cristina F. de Souza, Jaqueline P...
abstract: This study investigated if beetroot juice enhances post-exercise blood pressure reduction in hypertensive postmenopausal women. Acute beetroot juice intake did not alter blood pressure responses after aerobic exercise, despite increasing salivary nitrite levels.

title: Effect of milk fat globule membrane supplementation on motor unit adaptation following resistance training in older adults
authors: Kohei Watanabe, Aleš Holobar, Aya Tomita, Yukiko Mita
abstract: This study examined the effect of milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) supplementation on motor unit adaptation during resistance training in older adults. MFGM supplementation maintained higher motor unit firing rates and altered firing patterns compared to placebo.

title: Lower Dietary and Circulating Vitamin C in Middle- and Older-Aged Men and Women Are Associated with Lower Estimated Skeletal Muscle Mass
authors: Lucy N Lewis, Richard P G Hayhoe, Angela A Mulligan, Robert N Luben, Kay-Tee Khaw, Ailsa A Welch
abstract: This study examined the relationship between vitamin C intake and levels with skeletal muscle mass in middle-aged and older adults. Lower dietary and circulating vitamin C were associated with lower estimated skeletal muscle mass.

title: Melatonin Supplement Plus Exercise Effectively Counteracts the Challenges of Isoproterenol-Induced Cardiac Injury in Rats
authors: Md. Mahbubur Rahman, Dong Kwon Yang
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of exercise and melatonin on isoproterenol-induced cardiac injury in rats. The combination treatment effectively counteracted cardiac injury by preserving mitochondrial function and reducing oxidative stress.

title: Short-Term Beetroot Juice Supplementation Enhances Strength, Reduces Fatigue, and Promotes Recovery in Physically Active Individuals: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Crossover Trial
authors: Atef Salem, Achraf Ammar, Mohamed Kerkeni, Mohamed Ali Boujelbane, Ayse Merve Uyar, Leonard Moritz K...
abstract: Short-term beetroot juice supplementation was studied in resistance-trained males. It significantly increased repetitions completed and reduced muscle soreness, suggesting enhanced strength and recovery.

title: Metabolomic Analysis of Vitamin E Supplement Use in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
authors: Jungeun Lim, Hyokyoung G. Hong, Stephanie J. Weinstein, Mary C. Playdon, Amanda J. Cross, Rachael St...
abstract: This study analyzed serum metabolomic profiles in relation to vitamin E dosages from a cancer screening trial. Vitamin E supplementation was associated with changes in various metabolites, including steroid hormones, with sex-specific differences observed.

title: Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Performance and Fatigue in a 30-s All-Out Sprint Exercise: A Randomized, Double-Blind Cross-Over Study
authors: Eduardo Cuenca, Pablo Jodra, Alberto Pérez-López, Liliana G. González-Rodríguez, Sandro Fernandes da...
abstract: Beetroot juice supplementation was studied for its effects on a 30-second all-out sprint exercise. Beetroot juice improved peak and mean power output and reduced time to peak power, but did not affect fatigue.

title: Acute effects of combined supplementation of L-arginine and citrulline malate on aerobic, anaerobic, and CrossFit exercise performance
authors: Saranya Selvaraj, Leonidas Petridis, Hanna Majtényi, Henrietta Bartha, Ákos Tóth, Katinka Utczás, Ma...
abstract: This study examined the effects of L-arginine and citrulline malate supplementation on aerobic, anaerobic, and CrossFit performance in trained men. No significant performance improvements were found compared to placebo, except for a slightly faster peak power in one test.

title: Neither Beetroot Juice Supplementation nor Increased Carbohydrate Oxidation Enhance Economy of Prolonged Exercise in Elite Race Walkers
authors: Louise M. Burke, Rebecca Hall, Ida A. Heikura, Megan L. Ross, Nicolin Tee, Georgina L. Kent, Jamie W...
abstract: Beetroot juice and increased carbohydrate availability strategies were tested in elite race walkers. Neither approach improved exercise economy or substrate oxidation rates.

title: Optimizing vitamin supplementation via reference interval update of vitamins A, E, B1, and B6 using HPLC
authors: Andrea Caballero, Gonzalo Gonzalez-Silva, Pablo Gabriel-Medina, Marc Cuadros, Alfonso Ayora, Albert ...
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: Reference intervals for vitamins A, E, B1, and B6 were updated for an adult population using HPLC. The new values differ from manufacturer recommendations and may improve deficiency detection.

title: Sake Protein Supplementation Affects Exercise Performance and Biochemical Profiles in Power-Exercise-Trained Mice
authors: Yi-Ming Chen, Che-Li Lin, Li Wei, Yi-Ju Hsu, Kuan-Neng Chen, Chi-Chang Huang, Chin-Hsung Kao
abstract: A power exercise training program was used to study the effects of sake protein supplementation in mice. Sake protein supplementation enhanced anti-fatigue activity and improved biochemical profiles in trained mice.

title: The effect of almond consumption on elements of endurance exercise performance in trained athletes
authors: Muqing Yi, Jinde Fu, Lili Zhou, Hong Gao, Chenguang Fan, Jing Shao, Baohua Xu, Qirong Wang, Juntao L...
abstract: This study examined the effects of almond consumption on endurance exercise performance in trained athletes. Almonds improved cycling distance and enhanced carbohydrate utilization and oxygen efficiency during exercise compared to a placebo.

title: The Effects of Hyperhydrating Supplements Containing Creatine and Glucose on Plasma Lipids and Insulin Sensitivity in Endurance-Trained Athletes
authors: Thelma P. Polyviou, Yannis P. Pitsiladis, Carlos Celis-Morales, Benjamin Brown, John R. Speakman, Da...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of creatine, glycerol, and glucose supplements, with and without alpha lipoic acid, on endurance athletes. Supplementation increased plasma triglycerides and the triglyceride to HDL-cholesterol ratio, effects not mitigated by alpha lipoic acid.

title: Benfotiamine Supplementation Increases Thiamine in Muscle of Endurance-Trained Mice and Affects the Energy Metabolism
authors: Álisson C. Gonçalves, Jéssica F. Vieira, Ana Carolina N. Rodrigues, Eddie F. C. Murta, Júlio S. Marc...
abstract: Benfotiamine supplementation increased thiamine levels in endurance-trained mice. It altered muscle energy metabolism but did not improve endurance performance.

title: Effects of 4-Week Creatine Supplementation Combined with Complex Training on Muscle Damage and Sport Performance
authors: Chia-Chi Wang, Chu-Chun Fang, Ying-Hsian Lee, Ming-Ta Yang, Kuei-Hui Chan
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 4-week creatine supplementation with complex training on athletes. Creatine supplementation improved maximal strength and reduced muscle damage biomarkers compared to placebo.

title: High Baseline Vitamin C Levels Do Not Prevent a Positive Outcome of a Lifestyle Intervention
authors: Matthias Blüher, Michael Stumvoll, C. Ronald Kahn, Michael Ristow

title: Vitamin D status and its relation to exercise performance and iron status in young ice hockey players
authors: Joanna Orysiak, Joanna Mazur-Rozycka, John Fitzgerald, Michal Starczewski, Jadwiga Malczewska-Lenczo...
abstract: This study examined vitamin D levels in young ice hockey players and their relation to exercise performance and iron status. Vitamin D insufficiency was common, but no association was found with performance or iron markers.

title: Oral vitamin C supplementation to patients with myeloid cancer on azacitidine treatment: Normalization of plasma vitamin C induces epigenetic changes
authors: Linn Gillberg, Andreas D. Ørskov, Ammar Nasif, Hitoshi Ohtani, Zachary Madaj, Jakob W. Hansen, Nicol...
abstract: This study investigated oral vitamin C supplementation in myeloid cancer patients treated with azacitidine. Normalizing plasma vitamin C levels increased the 5hmC/5mC ratio, suggesting enhanced DNMTi effects.

title: Antioxidant-independent activities of alpha-tocopherol
authors: Matthew Chen, Mikel Ghelfi, Jia-Fei Poon, Nayeon Jeon, Natalie Boccalon, Michael Rubsamen, Stephen V...
abstract: A novel alpha-tocopherol analog lacking antioxidant activity was synthesized and studied. This analog modulated gene expression similarly to alpha-tocopherol, indicating antioxidant-independent biological activities.

title: Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Cognitive Function, Aerobic and Anaerobic Performances of Trained Male Taekwondo Athletes: A Pilot Study
authors: Hossein Miraftabi, Zahra Avazpoor, Erfan Berjisian, Amir Sarshin, Sajjad Rezaei, Raúl Domínguez, Rei...
abstract: This pilot study examined the effects of two doses of beetroot juice on taekwondo athletes' performance and cognitive function. The 400 mg dose of beetroot juice improved cognitive function after a performance test, though no significant performance differences were found.

title: Omega-3 dietary supplementation combined with exercise to keep telomere integrity in the liver of aged obese female mice
authors: Paola Elizabeth Gámez-Macías, Elisa Félix-Soriano, Neira Sáinz, Amelia Martí del Moral, Sonia García...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of omega-3 and exercise on liver telomere length in aged obese mice. Combined omega-3 and exercise prevented telomere shortening and improved antioxidant gene expression.

title: Effect of 10 Week Beta-Alanine Supplementation on Competition and Training Performance in Elite Swimmers
authors: Weiliang Chung, Greg Shaw, Megan E. Anderson, David B. Pyne, Philo U. Saunders, David J. Bishop, Lou...
abstract: This study investigated beta-alanine's effect on elite swimmers' training and competition performance over 10 weeks. Beta-alanine supplementation showed minimal impact on swimming performance in real-world settings.

title: Effects of Maltodextrin–Fructose Supplementation on Inflammatory Biomarkers and Lipidomic Profile Following Endurance Running: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Cross-Over Trial
authors: Stefano Righetti, Alessandro Medoro, Francesca Graziano, Luca Mondazzi, Serena Martegani, Francesco ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of maltodextrin–fructose supplementation on endurance runners. The supplementation significantly reduced post-exercise inflammation and metabolic stress.

title: Aging Brain: Prevention of Oxidative Stress by Vitamin E and Exercise
authors: Sambe Asha Devi
abstract: This study investigated how vitamin E and exercise affect the aging brain's cognitive decline. Findings suggest these interventions can slow decline by reducing oxidative stress and potentially acting synergistically.

title: Molecular control of endurance training adaptation in male mouse skeletal muscle
authors: Regula Furrer, Barbara Heim, Svenia Schmid, Sedat Dilbaz, Volkan Adak, Karl J. V. Nordström, Danilo ...
abstract: This study investigated the molecular changes in male mouse skeletal muscle following endurance training and acute exercise. Training significantly alters the muscle's transcriptional response to exercise, with factors like PGC-1α being crucial for adaptation.

title: Estimation of Vitamin C Intake Requirements Based on Body Weight: Implications for Obesity
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Gladys Block, Jens Lykkesfeldt
abstract: This study estimated vitamin C intake needs based on body weight. Higher body weight requires more vitamin C to maintain comparable plasma levels, suggesting current recommendations may be insufficient for heavier individuals.

title: Influence of beetroot juice supplementation on intermittent exercise performance
authors: Lee J. Wylie, Stephen J. Bailey, James Kelly, James R. Blackwell, Anni Vanhatalo, Andrew M. Jones
abstract: This study investigated the effect of beetroot juice supplementation on intermittent exercise performance in male team-sport players. Beetroot juice improved performance in short, repeated sprints with brief recovery, but not in longer intervals or those with extended recovery.

title: Bioavailability of vitamin C from kiwifruit in non-smoking males:
authors: determination of ‘healthy’ and ‘optimal’ intakes
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C absorption from kiwifruit in males. One kiwifruit daily achieved healthy plasma vitamin C levels, while two daily saturated plasma levels.

title: l -Arginine and Beetroot Extract Supplementation in the Prevention of Sarcopenia
authors: Alfredo Córdova-Martínez, Alberto Caballero-García, Hugo J. Bello, Antoni Pons-Biescas, David C. Nor...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of l-arginine and beetroot extract supplementation on muscle function in older adults over six weeks. Beetroot extract showed some benefits for women's muscle functionality and men's sprint performance, while l-arginine had no significant impact.

title: Acute beetroot juice supplementation enhances judo-specific performance, explosive power, and muscular strength in recreational adolescent judokas: a randomized crossover trial
authors: Abdullah Demirli, Eda Gökçelik, Abdorreza Eghbal Moghanlou, Muhammed Hüseyin Ocak, Merve Terzi, Emre...
abstract: Acute beetroot juice supplementation was studied in adolescent judokas. It enhanced judo-specific performance, explosive power, and muscular strength compared to a placebo.

title: Cordycepin combined with antioxidant effects improves fatigue caused by excessive exercise
authors: Chunfang Cheng, Shasha Zhang, Chong Chen, Yanchun Gong, Kaizhi Ding, Guoyin Li, Wei Jiang, Zhenyu Zh...
abstract: Cordycepin was studied for its anti-fatigue effects in mice subjected to excessive exercise. Cordycepin improved exercise performance and cognitive function by reducing fatigue metabolites and oxidative stress.

title: Effect of beetroot or beetroot plus vitamin C supplementation on cardiovascular function in patients with coronary artery disease: protocol for a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial
authors: Leila Sadat Bahrami, Mohsen Mohebaty, Seyyed Mostafa Arabi, Hamed Tabesh, Mohsen Nematy, Reza Rezvan...
abstract: This study investigates the effects of beetroot and beetroot plus vitamin C supplementation on cardiovascular function in patients with coronary artery disease. The trial will assess changes in various cardiovascular markers over four weeks of supplementation.

title: Acclimation Training Improves Endurance Cycling Performance in the Heat without Inducing Endotoxemia
authors: Joshua H. Guy, David B. Pyne, Glen B. Deakin, Catherine M. Miller, Andrew M. Edwards
abstract: This study investigated the effects of short-term heat training on endurance cycling performance and immune responses. Heat training improved cycling performance without causing significant immune system challenges.

title: Effects of exercise training with short‐duration intermittent hypoxia on endurance performance and muscle metabolism in well‐trained mice
authors: Junichi Suzuki
abstract: This study investigated the effects of intermittent hypoxia combined with exercise training on endurance in mice. Intermittent hypoxia enhanced endurance training and hybrid training by improving fatty acid and pyruvate oxidation.

title: Effect of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Aerobic Capacity in Female Athletes: A Randomized Controlled Study  †
authors: Jekaterina Neteca, Una Veseta, Inga Liepina, Katrina Volgemute, Maija Dzintare, Dmitry Babarykin
abstract: This study investigated the impact of beetroot juice on female endurance athletes' aerobic capacity. Beetroot juice supplementation significantly improved ventilation, respiratory equivalents, and heart rate, suggesting enhanced oxygen utilization.

title: Resistance Training Improves Muscle Strength and Function, Regardless of Protein Supplementation, in the Mid- to Long-Term Period after Gastric Bypass
authors: Gabriela S. Oliveira, Flávio T. Vieira, Fernando Lamarca, Ricardo M. Lima, Kênia M. B. Carvalho, Eli...
abstract: Resistance training was studied in individuals 2-7 years post-gastric bypass, with or without protein supplementation. Resistance training alone, or with protein, improved muscle strength and physical function.

title: Effect of a Diet Supplemented with α-Tocopherol and β-Carotene on ATP and Antioxidant Levels after Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion
authors: Pilar Codoñer-Franch, Pilar Muñiz, Esperanza Gasco, Juan V. Domingo, Victoria Valls-Belles
abstract: This study investigated the effects of α-tocopherol and β-carotene supplementation on rat livers subjected to ischemia-reperfusion. Supplementation improved antioxidant and energetic states, enhancing ATP recovery and altering antioxidant enzyme profiles.

title: Comparing Palm Oil, Tocotrienol-Rich Fraction and α-Tocopherol Supplementation on the Antioxidant Levels of Older Adults
authors: Nor Helwa Ezzah Nor Azman, Jo Aan Goon, Siti Madiani Abdul Ghani, Zalina Hamid, Wan Zurinah Wan Ngah
abstract: This study compared the effects of tocotrienol-rich fraction (TRF) and alpha-tocopherol (α-TF) on antioxidant levels in older adults. TRF supplementation significantly increased SOD activity, particularly in females, and improved the GSH/GSSG ratio in females.

title: Effects of branched-chain amino acid- and vitamin D-containing high-protein food supplementation plus exercise on elderly people with decreased physical functions
authors: Yoshihiro Nakamura, Takuji Yokoe, Koki Ouchi, Taro Funamoto, Hiroyuki Kimura, Koichiro Hamada, Hidek...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise plus a high-protein food supplement containing BCAAs and vitamin D on elderly individuals with decreased physical function. The combination of exercise and supplementation prevented declines in soft lean mass and improved physical performance compared to exercise alone or no intervention.

title: Association of vitamin E intake in diet and supplements with risk of dementia: A meta-analysis
authors: Rangyin Zhao, Xiaoyong Han, Hongxia Zhang, Jia Liu, Min Zhang, Weijing Zhao, Shangrong Jiang, Ruilin...
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the relationship between vitamin E intake and dementia risk. High vitamin E intake, from both diet and supplements, was found to significantly reduce the risk of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.

title: Performance and Submaximal Adaptations to Additional Speed-Endurance Training Vs. Continuous Moderate-Intensity Aerobic Training in Male Endurance Athletes
authors: Vincenzo Rago, Peter Krustrup, Magni Mohr
abstract: This study compared speed-endurance training (SET) with moderate-intensity training (MIT) in male endurance athletes. SET led to greater physiological demands and superior improvements in performance and running economy compared to MIT.

title: Effects of Acute Beetroot Juice Supplementation and Exercise on Cardiovascular Function in Healthy Men in Preliminary Study: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled, and Crossover Trial
authors: Xie Yuschen, Jae-Ho Choi, Jisoo Seo, Yerin Sun, Eunjoo Lee, Sung-Woo Kim, Hun-Young Park
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice supplementation combined with exercise on cardiovascular function in healthy men. Beetroot juice improved exercise capacity and cardiovascular function, including blood pressure and arterial stiffness, compared to a placebo.

title: Natural history of retinitis pigmentosa based on genotype, vitamin A/E supplementation, and an electroretinogram biomarker
authors: Jason Comander, Carol Weigel DiFranco, Kit Sanderson, Emily Place, Matthew Maher, Erin Zampaglione, ...
abstract: This study analyzed retinitis pigmentosa progression based on genotype, vitamin supplementation, and electroretinogram data. Genetic subtype and implicit time predict progression, vitamin E is harmful, and vitamin A's benefit is not generally supported.

title: Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on Deposition and Gene Expression Profiling of Abdominal Fat in Broiler Chickens
authors: Min Zhang, Jianlei Li, Yuting Zhu, Qiong Wu, Yan Li, Dingrui Huang, Zhending Gan, Lipeng Zhong, Jing...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin E's effect on broiler abdominal fat deposition and gene expression. Vitamin E supplementation reduced fat deposition and altered genes involved in fatty acid biosynthesis and lipid metabolism.

title: Effect of  Nigella sativa  Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Antioxidant Parameters: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: M. Ardiana, B. S. Pikir, A. Santoso, H. O. Hermawan, M. J. Al-Farabi
abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of Nigella sativa supplementation on oxidative stress. Nigella sativa supplementation increased superoxide dismutase levels but did not significantly affect malondialdehyde or total antioxidant capacity.

title: Effect of Dietary Nitrate and Anthocyanins on Anaerobic Exercise in Untrained Individuals
Low Carbohydrate, High Fat Diet Alters the Oral Microbiome without Negating the Nitrite Response to Beetroot Juice Supplementation
authors: Louise E. Cato, Alannah K. A. McKay, Joanna E. L’Heureux, Anni Vanhatalo, Andrew M. Jones, Christoph...
abstract: A low carbohydrate, high fat diet altered the oral microbiome in athletes. This diet did not negate the nitrite response to beetroot juice supplementation, indicating maintained nitrate reduction capacity.

title: Effects of vitamin E supplementation on some pregnancy health indices: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Parvin Bastani, Kobra Hamdi, Fatemeh Abasalizadeh, Nazli Navali
abstract: This randomized clinical trial investigated vitamin E supplementation's effects on pregnancy health indices. Supplementation did not significantly alter maternal or perinatal outcomes, including preeclampsia risk.

title: Human skeletal muscle ascorbate is highly responsive to changes in vitamin C intake and plasma concentrations 1 2 3
authors: Anitra C Carr, Stephanie M Bozonet, Juliet M Pullar, Jeremy W Simcock, Margreet CM Vissers
abstract: Skeletal muscle ascorbate levels were studied in response to vitamin C intake from kiwifruit. Muscle ascorbate concentrations significantly increased with intake and were more responsive than leukocytes.

title: Effects of dietary vitamin E on muscle vitamin E and fatty acid content in Aohan fine-wool sheep
authors: Kun Liu, Suyun Ge, Hailing Luo, Dubing Yue, Leyan Yan
source: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology
abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary vitamin E on muscle composition in Aohan fine-wool sheep. Vitamin E supplementation improved mutton's nutritional value by reducing saturated fatty acids and increasing monounsaturated fatty acids and conjugated linoleic acid, with optimal results at 200 IU/day.

title: Effect of supplemental vitamin E on the peripheral blood leukocyte population in Japanese Black calves
authors: Konosuke OTOMARU, Shun SAITO, Karura ENDO, Masayuki KOHIRUIMAKI, Hiromichi OHTSUKA
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: Supplemental vitamin E was given to Japanese Black calves, and their peripheral blood leukocyte populations were analyzed. Vitamin E supplementation increased the numbers of CD3+, CD4+, and CD21+ cells.

title: Circulating nitrate-nitrite reduces oxygen uptake for improving resistance exercise performance after rest time in well-trained CrossFit athletes
authors: Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Sergio Sánchez-Nuño, Lorena Molina-Raya, Teresa Carbonell, José Lui...
abstract: Circulating nitrate-nitrite from beetroot juice was studied in CrossFit athletes performing resistance exercise. Higher NOx reduced oxygen uptake during rest, improving squat performance.

title: Beetroot juice and vitamin C co-supplementation enhances anaerobic performance and reduces post-exercise glycemia in wrestlers: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial
authors: Maedeh Nojoumi; Ali Jafari; Alireza Hosseini Kakhki; Ali Jafarzadeh Esfehani; Hossein Rafiei; Chad K...
abstract: Wrestling, characterized by high-intensity intermittent efforts, demands exceptional anaerobic power and recovery capacity. Nitrate-rich beetroot juice (BRJ), supplemented with vitamin C, has emerged

title: Changes in Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, and Muscle Damage Markers Following Diet and Beetroot Juice Supplementation in Elite Fencers
authors: Lucyna Kozłowska, Olga Mizera, Jolanta Gromadzińska, Beata Janasik, Karolina Mikołajewska, Anna Mróz...
abstract: This study examined the effects of dietary recommendations and beetroot juice supplementation on elite fencers. Beetroot juice supplementation increased VO2max, which was linked to changes in muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Effects of a single dose of beetroot juice on cycling time trial performance at ventilatory thresholds intensity in male triathletes
authors: Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Guillem Palau-Salvà, Eduardo Cuenca, Arturo Muñoz-González, Pablo G...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of a single dose of beetroot juice on well-trained male triathletes. No significant improvements in performance or physiological variables were observed.

title: Skeletal muscle BMAL1 is necessary for transcriptional adaptation of local and peripheral tissues in response to endurance exercise training
authors: Mark R. Viggars, Hannah E. Berko, Stuart J. Hesketh, Christopher A. Wolff, Miguel A. Gutierrez-Monre...
abstract: Skeletal muscle BMAL1's role in exercise responses was studied using knockout mice and multi-omic analysis. Loss of muscle BMAL1 impairs acute exercise responses and alters training adaptations in muscle and peripheral tissues, potentially leading to inflammation.

title: Vitamin C Protects from Impairment of Memory Induced by E-Cigarette Aerosol Exposure
authors: Karem H. Alzoubi, Omar F. Khabour, Nour Al-Sawalha, Enaam M. Al Momany, Anan Jarab, Razan Haddad, Na...
abstract: This study investigated if Vitamin C protects rats from memory impairment caused by e-cigarette aerosol exposure. Vitamin C prevented memory deficits and restored oxidative stress markers and BDNF levels.

title: Beetroot Juice Produces Changes in Heart Rate Variability and Reduces Internal Load during Resistance Training in Men: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover
authors: Jose Manuel Jurado-Castro, David Casanova-Rodriguez, Julian Campos-Perez, Francisco Jesus Llorente-C...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice supplementation on autonomic nervous system responses during resistance training. Beetroot juice reduced internal training load and altered heart rate variability during exercise compared to a placebo.

title: Effects of dietary supplementation of vitamin-E and commercial probiotics on the innate immunity of  Labeo rohita  against  Aeromonas hydrophila  infection
authors: Leesa Priyadarsani, Thangapalam Jawahar Abraham, Harresh Adikesavalu, Gadadhar Dash, Talagunda Srini...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin E and probiotics on the innate immunity of Labeo rohita against Aeromonas hydrophila. Both supplements enhanced immunity, with vitamin E at 100 mg/kg proving more effective than probiotics at 5 g/kg.

title: Factors Associated with Increased Alpha-Tocopherol Content in Milk in Response to Maternal Supplementation with 800 IU of Vitamin E
authors: Amanda de Sousa Rebouças, Ana Gabriella Costa Lemos da Silva, Amanda Freitas de Oliveira, Lorena Tha...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of 800 IU of vitamin E supplementation on milk alpha-tocopherol levels in lactating women. Higher baseline milk vitamin E and dietary intake were found to be key factors influencing the supplementation's efficacy.

title: Vitamin E administration may decrease the incidence of pneumonia in elderly males
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: This study examined vitamin E's effect on pneumonia incidence in elderly male smokers. Vitamin E significantly reduced pneumonia risk in specific subgroups, particularly those who smoked fewer cigarettes and exercised.

title: Vitamin C: a misunderstood ally?
authors: Jiajia Ren, Xuting Jin, Ya Gao, Ruohan Li, Jiamei Li, Jingjing Zhang, Xiaochuang Wang, Gang Wang

title: Synergistic effects of exercise, cognitive training and vitamin D on gait performance and falls in mild cognitive impairment—secondary outcomes from the SYNERGIC trial
authors: Frederico Pieruccini-Faria, Surim Son, Guangyong Zou, Quincy J Almeida, Laura E Middleton, Nick W Br...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise, cognitive training, and vitamin D on gait and falls in older adults with mild cognitive impairment. Multimodal exercise and cognitive training improved gait speed and reduced falls, with benefits persisting at follow-up.

title: Nicotinic Acid Improves Endurance Performance of Mice Subjected to Treadmill Exercise
authors: Robert Ringseis, Denise K. Gessner, Anna M. Beer, Yvonne Albrecht, Gaiping Wen, Erika Most, Karsten ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of a high nicotinic acid diet combined with treadmill exercise on mouse endurance performance. The combined treatment significantly improved endurance and altered muscle fiber composition compared to exercise alone or control.

title: The JUMPFOOD study: additional effect of hydrolyzed collagen and vitamin C to exercise treatment for patellar tendinopathy (jumper’s knee) in athletes—study protocol for a double-blind randomized controlled trial
authors: L. van Dam, R. Terink, M. Mensink, R. J. de Vos, J. Zwerver
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating the effect of hydrolyzed collagen and vitamin C supplementation combined with exercise for patellar tendinopathy. The trial aims to determine if this combined approach improves pain and function compared to exercise alone.

title: Acute Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplements on Resistance Training: A Randomized Double-Blind Crossover
authors: Antonio Ranchal-Sanchez, Victor Manuel Diaz-Bernier, Candelaria Alonso De La Florida-Villagran, Fran...
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice's effects on resistance training performance. Beetroot juice supplementation increased the total number of repetitions performed during resistance training.

title: The effects of magnesium and vitamin E co-supplementation on parameters of glucose homeostasis and lipid profiles in patients with gestational diabetes
authors: Maryam Maktabi, Mehri Jamilian, Elaheh Amirani, Maryam Chamani, Zatollah Asemi
abstract: This study investigated magnesium and vitamin E co-supplementation in women with gestational diabetes. The supplementation significantly improved glucose control and lipid profiles, excluding HDL-cholesterol.

title: Single and combined effect of beetroot juice and caffeine intake on muscular strength, power and endurance performance in resistance-trained males
authors: Juan Jesús Montalvo-Alonso, Marta del Val-Manzano, Carmen Ferragut, David Valadés, Álvaro López-Sama...
abstract: This study examined the effects of beetroot juice and caffeine on resistance-trained males' strength, power, and endurance. Both supplements, individually and combined, improved back squat endurance but had no effect on bench press performance.

title: Effect of Beetroot Juice on Moderate-Intensity Exercise at a Constant Rating of Perceived Exertion
authors: JORDYN N. RIENKS, ANDREA A. VANDERWOUDE, ELIZABETH MAAS, ZACHARY M. BLEA, ANDREW W. SUBUDHI
abstract: This study investigated beetroot juice's effect on exercise at a constant perceived exertion. Beetroot juice did not alter oxygen consumption or work during self-regulated exercise, but did lower blood pressure and oxygen use at a fixed workload.

title: Influence of endurance and endurance–strength training on mineral status in women with abdominal obesity: a randomized trial
authors: Damian Skrypnik, Paweł Bogdański, Katarzyna Skrypnik, Edyta Mądry, Joanna Karolkiewicz, Monika Szuli...
abstract: Endurance and endurance-strength training were compared in abdominally obese women. Endurance-strength training showed more favorable effects on mineral balance, particularly for iron, magnesium, zinc, and copper.

title: Acute Effects of Beetroot Supplementation on Resistance Exercise Performance in Physically Active Men
authors: Maitê Yorioka Rodrigues; Monica Yuri Takito; Gabriel Albanese Kafouri; Rebeca Soares Pires; Felipe G...
abstract: Beetroot supplementation did not improve resistance exercise performance in physically active men. Nitrate intake did not significantly affect repetitions to failure, power output, heart rate, or perceived exertion during bench press and leg press. The study found no benefit for strength endurance from beetroot supplementation in trained individuals.

title: Resistance Training Is an Effective Tool against Metabolic and Frailty Syndromes
authors: Jan Sundell
abstract: Resistance training was studied for its effects on metabolic and frailty syndromes. It effectively reduces risk factors for metabolic syndrome and combats muscle and bone loss associated with frailty.

title: Effect of Beetroot Nitrate Supplementation on Nitric Oxide Pathways and Oxy-Inflammatory Biomarkers in Amateur Triathletes: A Randomized Cross-Over Pilot Study
authors: Simona Mrakic-Sposta; Alessandra Vezzoli; Mattia Parenza; Marcello Magno; Gennaro D’Angelo; Fabrizio...
abstract: Beetroot nitrate supplementation increased nitric oxide metabolites, iNOS, peroxynitrite, and IL-6 in triathletes. This occurred without significant changes in lipid oxidative damage markers. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and their impact on performance.

title: Likely Additive Ergogenic Effects of Combined Preexercise Dietary Nitrate and Caffeine Ingestion in Trained Cyclists
authors: Michal K. Handzlik, Michael Gleeson
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice and caffeine on cycling performance. Combined ingestion of beetroot juice and caffeine improved time to exhaustion and reduced perceived exertion compared to placebo or either supplement alone.

title: Vitamin C deficiency causes muscle atrophy and a deterioration in physical performance
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Tomoko Funakoshi, Tomofumi Yatsu, Kisaburo Nagata, Toshiro Aigaki, Shuichi Machida, ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C deficiency on skeletal muscle in mice. Vitamin C deficiency leads to muscle atrophy and reduced physical performance, which can be reversed with supplementation.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation combined with resistance exercise on body composition and metabolic variables in older women: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Illana Patricia da Silva Queiroz; Angélica Castilho Alonso; Vanderlei Carneiro da Silva; Adriana Mac...
abstract: This trial investigated vitamin D and resistance exercise in older women. The combination improved body composition and metabolic variables, suggesting a synergistic effect for muscle and bone health.

title: Beetroot Juice Enhances Nitrate Metabolism and Endothelial Function but Not Cardiovascular or Strength Performance in Bodybuilders with a History of Anabolic–Androgenic Steroid Abuse: A Crossover Trial
authors: Leonardo Santos L. da Silva; Leonardo Da Silva Gonçalves; Marcio F. Tasinafo Junior; Yaritza B. Alve...
abstract: Beetroot juice increased nitrate and nitrite levels and improved endothelial function in bodybuilders who used anabolic steroids. However, it did not improve blood pressure, heart rate, or strength performance in this population.

title: CYP1A2  Genotype and the Ergogenic Effect of Acute Caffeine Intake on Muscular Strength and Endurance Performance in Trained Individuals
authors: Juan Jesús Montalvo‐Alonso, Marta del Val‐Manzano, Iván Martín‐Rivas, Carmen Ferragut, David Valadés...
abstract: This study investigated if CYP1A2 genotype affects caffeine's ergogenic impact on strength and endurance in trained individuals. Caffeine improved performance, with benefits greatest in AA, intermediate in AC, and minimal in CC genotype carriers.

title: The Effect of Beetroot Ingestion on High-Intensity Interval Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Tak Hiong Wong, Alexiaa Sim, Stephen F. Burns
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated beetroot supplementation's effects on high-intensity interval training performance. Beetroot supplementation showed no significant improvement in peak or mean power output during HIIT or SIT.

title: Understanding the effects of beetroot juice intake on CrossFit performance by assessing hormonal, metabolic and mechanical response: a randomized, double-blind, crossover design
authors: Manuel Vicente Garnacho-Castaño, Guillem Palau-Salvà, Noemí Serra-Payá, Mario Ruiz-Hermosel, Marina ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of beetroot juice on CrossFit performance, measuring hormonal, metabolic, and mechanical responses. Beetroot juice improved performance when rest was provided between exercises, but increased cortisol, reduced oxygen saturation, and heightened muscular fatigue.

title: Effects of Beetroot Juice on Recovery of Muscle Function and Performance between Bouts of Repeated Sprint Exercise
authors: Tom Clifford, Bram Berntzen, Gareth W. Davison, Daniel J. West, Glyn Howatson, Emma J. Stevenson
abstract: Beetroot juice was given to male team-sports players for 3 days after repeated sprint tests. Beetroot juice improved recovery of jump height and reactive strength index between sprint bouts.

title: Right heart exercise-training-adaptation and remodelling in endurance athletes
authors: Valeria Conti, Filippo Migliorini, Marco Pilone, María I. Barriopedro, Juan José Ramos-Álvarez, Fran...
abstract: This systematic review examined right heart structural and functional changes in endurance athletes. Findings indicate that right heart remodeling in athletes is associated with age, body surface area, and training intensity.

title: Acute Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Isometric Muscle Strength, Rate of Torque Development and Isometric Endurance in Young Adult Men and Women: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Controlled Cross-Over Pilot Study
authors: David Poredoš, Zala Jenko Pražnikar, Žiga Kozinc
abstract: This study examined beetroot juice's effects on isometric strength and endurance in young adults. Beetroot juice did not improve maximal strength but enhanced endurance and torque development rate in men, not women.

title: Effects of blood flow restriction training on aerobic capacity and performance in endurance athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Zekai Zhang, Xuejiao Gao, Lang Gao
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated blood flow restriction (BFR) training's effects on endurance athletes. BFR training moderately improves aerobic capacity and endurance performance, and significantly enhances muscle strength.

title: Low Vitamin C Concentrations in Patients with Community-Acquired Pneumonia Resolved with Pragmatic Administration of Intravenous and Oral Vitamin C
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Emma Vlasiuk, Masuma Zawari, Amy Scott-Thomas, Malina Storer, Michael Maze, Stephen ...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C levels in community-acquired pneumonia patients and the effect of supplementation. Vitamin C supplementation effectively restored depleted levels in these patients.
